artigo.texto: At the OCP Global Summit 2026, we presented a compressor architecture designed around a problem that does not get enough attention: what happens when the cooling plant is not running at peak load. Most data center cooling conversations focus on peak capacity. But most cooling plants spend a significant share of their operating hours nowhere near it. Mild weather, seasonal transitions, and cold-plate supply temperatures rising toward 45°C push the system toward low-lift conditions, where the pressure ratio across the compressor is low but refrigerant flow remains high. This is where conventional compressor architectures lose their efficiency advantage, and where operators quietly burn energy they do not need to. As the industry moves toward air-cooled systems to reduce water dependence, the compressor faces a wider operating envelope than ever before. Conventional two-stage centrifugal compressors lock both impellers to a single shaft speed, and at their design point they perform well. But the fixed speed ratio between stages limits how precisely the pressure split can be optimized, and at low lift near the free-cooling boundary, pushing high refrigerant flow through two compression stages when only one is needed creates parasitic losses at exactly the operating points where the plant spends much of its time. Decoupling the Rotors The architecture we presented takes a different approach. Instead of coupling both impellers to a single shaft, the design uses two independent magnetic-bearing rotors, each driven by its own motor and variable-speed drive. The two stages can run at different speeds, and the second stage can be isolated entirely when it is not needed. This gives operators two distinct operating regions. Under high ambient temperatures, both stages run together with independently tuned speeds, improving stage matching and peak isentropic efficiency by 2% to 3% over a coupled-speed reference. Near the free-cooling threshold, integrated bypass valves switch the system to single-stage operation, eliminating redundant compression work. At representative duty points, this reduces compressor power from 80 kW to 48 kW at the same cooling capacity, a 40% reduction, while improving low-lift efficiency by up to 15% and increasing usable low-lift flow by 70%. At a pressure ratio of 1.6 and 22% of reference inlet flow, the architecture reaches 81% isentropic efficiency without inlet guide vanes, compared with 73% for a coupled-speed compressor fitted with inlet guide vanes. Keeping Cooling Continuous During Mode Transitions For facilities that prioritize refrigerant-pump free cooling backed by mechanical cooling, the transition between modes is where things can go wrong. In liquid-cooled AI environments, even brief interruptions can trigger server thermal throttling or downtime. The risk during a mechanical-to-free-cooling transition is well understood: rapid depressurization can cause stored liquid to flash at the pump inlet, starving flow and creating a transient capacity gap. The independent-speed architecture addresses this by preconditioning the refrigerant in single-stage mode before pump takeover, reducing inlet mixture volume by 78.4% compared with a direct two-stage-to-pump handover. The reverse transition carries its own risk. Conventional compressors require an iterative startup sequence, slowing condenser fans to raise condensing pressure before the compressor can reach its operating envelope. Single-stage startup eliminates that delay: the compressor begins operating at a low pressure ratio and builds capacity before ramping up to the second stage, while also supporting faster restarts after power restoration. Fitting Two Shafts into One Footprint A conventional dual-shaft arrangement would be approximately 25% longer than a single-shaft unit, and in space-constrained air-cooled chillers, that extra length comes directly out of the space available for heat exchangers, fans, and service access. The architecture we developed maintains the axial footprint of a conventional single-shaft compressor by placing outboard magnetic bearings inside volute recesses and combining seals, sensors, and backup bearings into integrated function units, alongside compact motors rated up to 70 kW at 41,000 rpm. At the OCP Global Summit 2026, our compressor technology received the “2026 GW-Scale Open AIDC Excellent Technical Presentation Award,” recognizing its contribution to more efficient and reliable thermal architectures for next-generation AI data centers. From Compressor Innovation to Full-Chain Cooling A compressor is only one part of the cooling system. Clivet brings this core cooling-source technology into a full-chain liquid cooling approach that spans cooling sources, high-capacity coolant distribution units (CDUs), fan walls and terminal units. Designed to prioritize free cooling while retaining dependable mechanical-cooling backup, this integrated portfolio supports scalable thermal management across different climates and AI infrastructure requirements. At this year’s OCP Global Summit, Midea also appeared in the list of participating companies in the NVIDIA MGX ecosystem. The inclusion highlights Midea’s growing role in the broader AI computing infrastructure ecosystem, where effective thermal management increasingly depends on coordination across equipment, systems and industry platforms. As AI facilities move toward gigawatt-scale computing, we see the next step as bringing core cooling innovations together with system-level engineering and open ecosystem collaboration. Building on Midea and Clivet’s “equipment + systems + ecosystem” approach, our goal is to help deliver more efficient, reliable and sustainable cooling infrastructure for the next generation of AI data centers. For more information about Clivet's liquid cooling portfolio for AI data centers, visit www.clivet.com.

artigo.texto: IREN Co-CEO Daniel Roberts Says Firm’s Data Centers Carry No Debt As Funding Worries Hit Stock - After recent pressure on the IREN stock, co-CEO Daniel Roberts said that the company's data centers are supported fully by cash, and the company had no debt against assets. - Under recent three-year contracts, customer prepayments cover 45% to 55% of GPU expenses, Roberts said. - IREN's Microsoft agreement covered 96% of GPU expenses, with prepayments at 6%, and non-investment payment-grade customers paid 9%. Shares of IREN Limited (IREN) edged lower in pre-market trading on Tuesday after co-CEO Daniel Roberts said that the company's data centers did not carry any debt. Roberts responded to investors' concern over how the artificial intelligence (AI) cloud providers will fund their expansion. Roberts said on X that IREN has paid for their data center construction in cash so far. Adding to it, he said that the sites can support their own financing once they come online with contracted customers. Robert laid out the process step by step. Customers must first sign multi-year take-or-pay contracts, which require payment whether or not they use the capacity. On recent three-year deals, he said prepayments covered 45% to 55% of the cost of the graphics processing units (GPUs).https://x.com/danroberts0101/status/2112200081034129419?s=20 He added that lenders mostly fund the rest, with the GPUs serving as collateral. Robert added that Iren's Microsoft (MSFT) contract was supported by an A-rated facility at 6% or so. That, plus prepayments, accounts for 96% of the GPU spending. One customer without an investment-grade rating at Iren's McKenzie site in British Columbia was borrowing at a fixed 9%. The loan and prepayment more than pay for the whole cost of the GPU, the co-CEO added. He acknowledged that future debt will price at whatever the market charges. But he said a payback of about 2 years on recent contracts means "a wider spread barely moves the economics." Demand Outruns Build Capacity According to Roberts, customer demand exceeds what IREN can build. The company's 2026 capacity is largely sold out, he added, saying recent 3-year contracts are priced at more than double last year's level. Demand for capacity arriving in 2027 is several times oversubscribed, and discussions on 2028 have begun. The holdup in the industry is not signing deals, he said. Getting GPUs online is the issue, as announced capacity keeps sleeping across the sector. Pressure On Neocoloud Stocks Continue Neoclouds, the specialized AI cloud providers, have been under pressure through the past week. The stock has been down over 20% over the past week. Investors became increasingly worried after debt pressures at CoreWeave (CRWV) and a research firm warned that over 80% of neoclouds might no longer be able to operate independently by 2030. Retail Chatter For IREN Surges IREN stock was down over 4% in pre-market trade, trading at $26. On Stocktwits retail sentiment around IREN remained in the ‘extremely bullish’ zone, with ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day. According to platform data, chatter around IREN has been up over 952% over the past 30 days. One user on Stocktwits said that the IREN stock had erased all of the previous day's gain, and it would need to rise 70% to reach above $46 again.

artigo.texto: CATL Unveils Dual-Electric Range Extension Battery to Accelerate Electric Heavy-Duty Truck Adoption BEIJING, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CATL today unveiled the innovative dual-electric range extension battery and the latest generation of heavy-duty battery-swapping solution to accelerate the electrification of road freight transportation. Competition in electric heavy-duty trucking is moving beyond technical specifications toward full-lifecycle value. While battery swapping has made energy replenishment faster and more predictable, concerns about battery utilization, operating costs and residual vehicle value continue to affect fleet economics. To address these challenges, CATL combines its dual-electric range extension battery with QIJI's strategy of standardization, new infrastructure and a full commercial ecosystem, bringing battery swapping and industry-wide collaboration together to accelerate heavy-duty truck electrification. A Dual-Electric Approach to Range Extension CATL's dual-electric range extension battery combines two independent yet complementary battery systems. The main battery uses QIJI's standardized chassis-mounted swappable battery to maximize efficiency. A behind-the-cab range-extension power system, currently equipped with a 77kWh battery capable of 3C charging, provides backup power. Together, the systems maintain uninterrupted power delivery and provide redundancy for demanding operating conditions. - Dual-System Power Redundancy In conventional battery-swapping trucks, drivers often return for a swap with unused capacity because they are reluctant to run the battery low. Backup power from the range-extension battery increases the main battery's depth of discharge (DOD) from approximately 70% to over 95%, allowing it to be returned at less than 5% state of charge (SOC). At this threshold, CATL's seamless switching technology transfers power delivery to the range-extension battery within milliseconds, maintaining a continuous and stable power supply. - "1+X" Architecture and Independent Upgrades The system uses a "1+X" architecture. One standardized main battery maintains compatibility with the QIJI battery-swapping network, while the range-extension battery can be customized for specific conditions with options including ultra-high energy density, low-temperature resistance for cold climates, or ultra-high power. The two battery systems can be developed and upgraded independently to meet their respective technical and operational requirements. - Flexible Leasing and Battery Asset Management The independently owned on-board range-extension battery stays with the vehicle as an asset throughout its service life, reducing reliance on immediate access to a swapping station. The main battery can be leased according to seasonal freight demand, helping fleets reduce rental costs during quieter periods and manage battery assets more flexibly. This architecture combines the benefits of standardization with flexible vehicle configurations, making electric heavy-duty trucks more practical and economically viable across a wider range of applications. QIJI Builds a Shared Battery Swapping Ecosystem QIJI complements these improvements with a three-pillar strategy of standardization, new infrastructure and a full commercial ecosystem. It seeks to speed heavy-duty truck electrification with a value-chain ecosystem co-created by all stakeholders, where benefits are shared collectively. - Standardization Supports Wider Adoption To accommodate a wider range of truck models and operating conditions, QIJI has introduced the 260# (432 kWh) and 300# (513 kWh) standardized battery-swapping blocks alongside the existing 75# block. The system enables battery swaps in just five minutes, with a 99.99% first-time success rate, helping fleets minimize downtime and maintain operational efficiency. QIJI has also pioneered a battery-as-a-service (BaaS) model in which customers pay for the net energy charged rather than the energy discharged. This allows customers to retain the value of energy recovered through regenerative braking, reducing per-kWh battery rental costs for users on basic plans by up to 20%. Flexible battery leasing options allow customers to tailor rental periods to their needs, from second-hand vehicle transitions to seasonal demand. This will minimize idle costs and offer more flexible options for off-season downtime, further helping fleets manage operating costs. - New Infrastructure Improves Resource Efficiency QIJI aims to make better use of four critical resources in long-haul freight: time, land, payload capacity and grid electricity. Rapid battery swapping reduces waiting times, while efficient station layouts serve more vehicles within the same footprint. Battery capacity is matched to transport needs, and centralized, coordinated charging makes better use of grid electricity. These measures aim to improve both resource efficiency and operational returns. CATL plans to deploy 900 battery-swapping stations by the end of 2026 and 2,000 by 2027, with a long-term target of 10,000 stations nationwide in collaboration with its partners. By connecting major freight corridors through a coordinated swapping network, QIJI aims to improve the efficiency and commercial viability of electric heavy-duty trucking. - A Commercial Ecosystem Supports the Full Vehicle Lifecycle QIJI connects truck manufacturers, financial institutions, insurers, channel partners and aftermarket service providers across the vehicle lifecycle, from purchase and operation to maintenance and resale, working together to build a comprehensive ecosystem of integrated products and services. QIJI has introduced two partnership models: Battery Asset Service Partners and Energy Replenishment Service Partners. These models allow partners to participate in battery asset services and energy replenishment, extending their role beyond one-off vehicle sales to ongoing operations. artigo.texto: Trump defende que empresas de data centers paguem "dividendos" às comunidades Donald Trump defendeu que empresas de data centers paguem "dividendos" às comunidades locais para reduzir a oposição popular gerada pelo alto consumo de água e energia dessas instalações de IA. O ex-presidente também exigiu que esses empreendimentos gerem sua própria eletricidade e repassem o excedente à rede elétrica. A pressão pública sobre o setor já levou iniciativas de compartilhamento de recursos por empresas como a Anthropic e por Elon Musk. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta quarta-feira que as empresas que constroem data centers deveriam pagar um "dividendo" às comunidades onde eles estão localizados, caso queiram que esses empreendimentos sejam bem-aceitos. "Tenho acompanhado o processo de perto e percebi que data centers que eram altamente impopulares em determinada região tornaram-se extremamente populares quando um acordo financeiro foi fechado", disse Trump em uma postagem no Truth Social. Os data centers, que impulsionam o avanço da IA, tornaram-se um ponto de tensão política em comunidades por todo o país, devido às grandes quantidades de água e energia que consomem, com a oposição unindo eleitores de todas as tendências ideológicas. O governo Trump, que priorizou o rápido desenvolvimento da IA para competir com a China, também observou a mudança no sentimento dos eleitores. "Exigi que os novos e grandes -- em alguns casos, gigantescos -- data centers produzam sua própria eletricidade e doem ou vendam qualquer excedente de volta à comunidade local ou à rede elétrica", disse Trump em sua postagem. Trump afirmou em fevereiro que as grandes empresas de tecnologia devem construir suas próprias usinas de energia para seus data centers, a fim de proteger os consumidores do aumento nas contas. A gigante de IA Anthropic e o bilionário Elon Musk apresentaram, nos últimos dias, planos para compartilhar parte dos frutos do boom da inteligência artificial. A criadora dos modelos Claude anunciou no fim de semana que está destinando 5% de suas ações a um novo fundo para o "bem público", enquanto Musk se comprometeu na segunda-feira a doar uma ação da SpaceX para "cada criança nos Estados Unidos", defendendo essas distribuições diretas à medida que o setor em expansão enfrenta o escrutínio público.

A certificate of attendance will be offered. Data center construction is colliding with a power bottleneck. Interconnection queues now stretch past five years in major markets, and developers are responding with microgrids, battery energy storage systems, and bring-your-own-power strategies that push more electrical infrastructure inside the fence line. For engineers and contractors working on these projects, that shift changes what conduit specification looks like, and raises new questions around grounding, fire code compliance, and installation at scale. Join Matt Fredericks, VP of Sales and Marketing at Champion Fiberglass®, for a practical look at how these power strategies are reshaping underground electrical infrastructure. Drawing on real project data and current code requirements, Matt will walk through what's driving these builds, where conduit decisions carry the most risk, and what tools are available to help your team plan with confidence. What you'll learn: - How microgrids, BESS, and BYOP strategies are changing data center power delivery, and what's driving developers toward each approach - The specific conduit challenges each strategy introduces, from fault resistance to fire resistance requirements - How grounding and bonding work with nonmetallic conduit systems - Specification guidance for medium-voltage duct banks and multi-circuit runs - Lessons from real data center installations, including common field pitfalls to avoid - How tools like BIM modeling and the Champ Pull® calculator can streamline design and installation Speaker Sponsored by:

artigo.texto: ‘No question’ data centers will be considered critical infrastructure, top House intel Dem says Rep. Jim Himes, D-Conn., said the AI-focused facilities are going to be even more critical than their traditional data center counterparts because “so much more functionality is going to rely on their health and existence.” The growing web of data centers across the United States that are needed to power artificial intelligence technologies is destined to be deemed critical infrastructure, according to the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee. During an event at the Brookings Institution on Wednesday, Rep. Jim Himes, D-Conn. — the powerful House panel’s ranking member — said “I think there’s no question” that data centers will be considered critical infrastructure in the future, adding that “they're going to be even more important than the network data centers that we've been living with for 40 years now because so much more functionality is going to rely on their health and existence.” U.S. critical infrastructure services are currently divided into 16 sectors, which range in size and scope from water and wastewater facilities to IT infrastructure and financial services. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency oversees the security of these sectors, which have been deemed so vital to U.S. interests that their destruction could have national security or other serious repercussions. Although AI data centers already underpin some of the critical infrastructure, they are not yet deemed to be a standalone sector. Ongoing global conflicts, however, have highlighted the importance of these new data centers, with the facilities increasingly becoming military targets. In March, Iran hit Amazon Web Services data centers in the United Arab Emirates and a third commercial data center in Bahrain with drones as Tehran moved to target U.S. tech companies’ regional interests as part of the war. In recent weeks, Russia and Ukraine have also traded strikes on data centers within each country. Himes said securing U.S. data centers will ultimately result in the need for a “robust compute infrastructure,” with technologies likely having to “fragment and disperse” key services so that “critical functions are redundant and protected.” “They haven't had to think in those terms quite yet because this is a new thing,” he added. “But as more and more of the agents, and as more and more of the commercial economy depends on these things, they will start to look more like JP Morgan's resilience centers than they look like today's data centers.” JPMorganChase launched its $1.5 trillion, 10-year Security and Resiliency Initiative last year to help drive investments in industries deemed critical to U.S. national and economic security interests. The firm announced on Monday that it has invested $5 billion in startups over the first year of its effort, although it did not disclose most of the recipients of those funds. AI data center construction has become increasingly controversial, with some Americans and lawmakers criticizing the facilities’ power use and water consumption. Although the House overwhelmingly passed bipartisan legislation, known as the Ratepayer Protection Act, last month that would push the companies building data centers to pay for their electrical use, Himes said the measure “wasn't meaningful or substantive” and noted that it hasn’t been voted on yet in the Senate. Himes said data center backlash is “driven by an eminently solvable problem,” which is addressing the underlying question of, “‘How do we equitably divide up the costs of building the compute?’” He added, however, that continuing data center construction is inevitable, saying that “the experts tell me that the underlying demand for compute still looks infinite, and as long as that is a true fact, the build will happen.”

artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no CEO do HSBC alerta que boom da IA não torna todos os data centers bons investimentos Publicado 20/10/2026 • 10:07 | Atualizado há 21 horas KEY POINTS Pexels A inteligência artificial (IA) é uma tecnologia transformadora que merece investimentos, mas os investidores precisam ser criteriosos ao escolher projetos de data centers, segundo o presidente-executivo de um dos maiores bancos do mundo. Em entrevista a Dan Murphy, da CNBC, nesta terça-feira (20), Georges Elhedery, CEO do HSBC, classificou a inteligência artificial como “um importante facilitador para reformular e reinventar todos os nossos negócios e atividades”. “Ela vai devolver muito poder aos nossos colegas por causa do nível de produtividade que proporciona. Portanto, será transformadora, e estamos certamente em uma jornada para adotá-la”, afirmou. Segundo ele, a IA também ajudará a “reformular o banco”. No entanto, ao abordar os investimentos em infraestrutura que sustenta essa tecnologia, Elhedery recomendou cautela, em vez de uma aposta indiscriminada no setor. Leia também: HSBC amplia receita e mantém lucro estável no 1º trimestre, com alta de depósitos e pressão de custos “É preciso ser seletivo”, afirmou. “É necessário avaliar a qualidade dos contratos de locação e os preços estabelecidos nesses contratos. Nem todos apresentam um nível de qualidade que permita sustentá-los com confiança. Alguns podem ser mais desafiadores.” O HSBC foi classificado pela S&P Global, no ano passado, como o sétimo maior banco do mundo e o maior credor da Europa, com ativos próximos de US$ 3 trilhões. Com sede em Londres, a instituição atua tanto no financiamento quanto na operação de data centers. Em seu relatório anual de 2025, o HSBC afirmou que pretende se tornar “o banco líder para ecossistemas de transição de rápido crescimento”, destacando que sua carteira de clientes abrange setores como data centers e inteligência artificial. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC Os complexos de data centers abrigam os servidores que sustentam a IA e a computação em nuvem. Nos últimos anos, o setor passou por uma expansão bilionária, impulsionada pela crescente demanda por capacidade computacional. Segundo a consultoria McKinsey, os gastos globais com data centers podem atingir US$ 7 trilhões até 2030. Para financiar a construção dessas instalações, grandes empresas de tecnologia têm recorrido cada vez mais ao crédito privado e à emissão de dívidas. O endividamento relacionado à IA, porém, está se tornando uma fonte de tensão nos mercados financeiros. O custo do capital está aumentando, enquanto empresas acumulam grandes volumes de dívida na corrida para financiar o desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial e a expansão da infraestrutura de data centers. Durante o GZERO Summit, organizado pela LSEG e pelo Eurasia Group em Londres no início deste mês, Mohamed El-Erian, principal consultor econômico da Allianz e ex-CEO da PIMCO, destacou a disputa por financiamento entre governos e empresas ligadas à IA como uma fonte de pressão sobre os mercados de títulos de dívida. Leia também: HSBC impulsiona Bolsas da Europa após elevar meta de rentabilidade “Os governos estão tomando emprestado o que precisam tomar, além de refinanciarem suas dívidas a taxas de juros mais altas”, afirmou. “E temos as grandes empresas de tecnologia que operam em larga escala na nuvem, que captaram US$ 200 bilhões em financiamento por meio de títulos de dívida no ano passado e provavelmente vão captar US$ 1 trilhão dessa forma neste ano. Elas não são sensíveis aos rendimentos. Não são sensíveis aos spreads de crédito, porque estão apostando em algo verdadeiramente transformador.” Os rendimentos dos títulos de dívida emitidos por diversas grandes economias atingiram, em 2026, os níveis mais elevados em várias décadas. O movimento ocorre em meio a preocupações com os elevados déficits públicos e o aumento do endividamento, além dos temores de que a inflação permaneça persistente e os bancos centrais adotem posturas mais rigorosas. No início deste ano, o JPMorgan Chase estimou que a emissão de dívidas relacionadas à inteligência artificial poderá alcançar US$ 4,1 trilhões até o fim da década, à medida que empresas de data centers e outros negócios ligados à IA ampliam os investimentos para expandir sua capacidade. 🔷 Canal 562 ClaroTV+ | Canal 562 Sky | Canal 592 Vivo | Canal 187 Oi | Operadoras regionais 🔷 TV SINAL ABERTO: parabólicas canal 562 🔷 ONLINE: www.timesbrasil.com.br | YouTube 🔷 FAST Channels: Samsung TV Plus, LG Channels, TCL Channels, Pluto TV, Roku, Zapping | Novos Streamings Este conteúdo foi fornecido pela CNBC Internacional e a responsabilidade exclusiva pela tradução para o português é do Times Brasil. artigo.texto: Pará tem potencial para liderar restauração florestal com créditos de carbono Conciliar a produção agrícola com a conservação das florestas, ampliar a restauração de áreas degradadas e transformar a preservação ambiental em oportunidades econômicas estão entre os desafios e as possibilidades para o Pará. Em entrevista ao Grupo Liberal, Leonardo Sobral, diretor de Florestas e Restauração do Imaflora (Instituto de Manejo e Certificação Florestal e Agrícola), destaca o potencial do estado para avançar nessa agenda por meio de incentivos econômicos, do mercado de carbono, da bioeconomia e das concessões florestais para restauração. O especialista também ressalta a importância de valorizar os produtos da floresta em pé e de fortalecer iniciativas que conciliem conservação ambiental, produção sustentável e geração de renda. * Repórter: Jéssica Nascimento Por Liberal Entrevista

artigo.texto: BYD Pairs European Luxury Push With 3,000 Chargers as Shares Languish Near Yearly Low Published on 10/20/2026 at 03:31 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD is betting that premium badges and its own charging infrastructure can lift its fortunes in Europe, even as its share price continues to sag. At the Paris Motor Show, the Chinese group rolled out its Denza marque with a technology-led pitch for what it calls intelligent luxury — a direct challenge to Europe's established premium names. The display came alongside the seven-seat ATTO 8 flagship SUV and the second generation of its Blade battery. Charging is central to the pitch. BYD plans to build 3,000 fast-charging stations across Europe by the end of 2027, a move aimed at winning drivers over to its rapid-charging technology. The company is also scaling up its local footprint: deputy chairwoman Stella Li told Bloomberg that European headcount will soon pass 10,000, with roughly 40,000 employees targeted in the region by 2030. A Two-Pronged Expansion The European push runs in parallel with a broader build-out beyond vehicle sales. BYD Energy Storage announced a global after-sales service network for battery storage systems, built around nine operations and maintenance centres and more than 200 field engineers. Additional sites in South Africa and Bulgaria are slated for 2027, and over 100 R&D specialists are tied into the network — a signal that BYD intends to stay close to commercial customers long after installation. At home, the group keeps widening its lineup. The Da Han EV, a new flagship sedan for the Dynasty range, launched on 13 October with a 1,000-volt architecture and a CLTC range of up to 1,008 kilometres; the entry version is priced at 235,900 yuan. BYD also introduced the second generation of its Seagull compact EV in China, according to media reports, shoring up its volume base. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? September Sales and a Hybrid Trade Deal Those model launches land in a testing market. BYD's September 2026 production and sales report showed 463,561 vehicles sold and 463,864 built during the month. Sales through September reached 3,131,576 units, down 3.9% on the same period a year earlier. Trade policy adds another variable. BYD has reportedly backed an agreement between China and the European Union on hybrid vehicle trade, though Reuters noted that such a deal — by capping exports of Chinese hybrid and plug-in hybrid models — could create headwinds for manufacturers. Details on how the arrangement would work in practice have not been disclosed. Investors Stay on the Sidelines The market has yet to be moved by the operational announcements. The stock closed Monday at EUR 8.30, down 0.5%, and slipped a further 0.1% to EUR 8.33 in today's session. That leaves the shares down 22% since the start of the year and well below the 52-week high of EUR 12.30 touched in mid-April. A nearer-term catalyst is on the calendar: the supervisory board meets on 29 October 2026 to review third-quarter results. For now, BYD is sticking to its strategy of putting technological innovation and higher-margin segments such as Denza at the forefront of its international drive. artigo.texto: A busca por autonomia, segurança operacional e independência da rede elétrica tradicional tornou-se uma prioridade crescente para brasileiros, empresas e produtores rurais. De acordo com um levantamento recente da Descarbonize Soluções, empresa especializada em transição energética, os últimos 12 meses registraram mais de 50 mil consultas relacionadas a soluções de armazenamento de eletricidade no Google, representando um salto anual de 48%. O destaque absoluto da temporada fica por conta dos Sistemas de Armazenamento em Baterias (BESS, na sigla em inglês), que ultrapassaram 104 mil buscas e dispararam impressionantes 120% no período. Em termos de volume total, as tradicionais baterias estacionárias mantêm a liderança isolada, acumulando 248 mil pesquisas online. Segundo dados pesquisados pela redação do CenárioMT, o estado de Mato Grosso figura com destaque entre os dez estados brasileiros que mais demonstraram interesse pelo tema do armazenamento avançado de energia (BESS), refletindo a necessidade do agronegócio e das indústrias locais em buscar estabilidade frente aos desafios climáticos e gargalos de distribuição. Fatores econômicos e leilões da Aneel impulsionam o setor O aquecimento do mercado não é impulsionado apenas pelo desejo de autossuficiência, mas também por importantes marcos regulatórios e econômicos. A Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) colocou em consulta pública os primeiros leilões voltados especificamente ao armazenamento de energia no país, com licitações agendadas para os dias 2 e 4 de dezembro de 2026. Além disso, um fator histórico mudou o jogo: pela primeira vez, o custo dessas estruturas de armazenamento tornou-se inferior ao das usinas termelétricas a gás. Dados da BloombergNEF apontam que, desde 2022, os investimentos em instalações de porte utilitário caíram mais de 50%, com uma retração de 27% registrada apenas no último ano, tornando a tecnologia comercialmente viável em larga escala. Radiografia do interesse no país O mapeamento das buscas online — realizado entre setembro de 2025 e agosto de 2026 — avaliou os termos mais procurados por estado proporcionalmente à sua população: - Baterias estacionárias: Lideram em volume absoluto com 248 mil pesquisas (+22%). - Bess: Aceleração recorde de 120% e mais de 104 mil buscas. - Bateria para energia solar e kits off-grid: Mantêm crescimento expressivo, com altas entre 22% e 53%. No ranking dos estados que mais buscaram por BESS, Santa Catarina lidera o interesse — embalada por investimentos recentes do BNDES de R$ 280 milhões para a construção de uma fábrica de baterias em Itajaí —, seguida por Distrito Federal e Paraná. São Paulo ocupa o quarto lugar, enquanto Mato Grosso, Espírito Santo, Rio de Janeiro, Goiás, Rio Grande do Sul e Minas Gerais completam o top 10 nacional. Impacto para o agronegócio e grandes setores em Mato Grosso Para o ecossistema produtivo de Mato Grosso, onde a alta performance agrícola exige fornecimento elétrico contínuo para sistemas de irrigação, armazenagem de grãos, aviários e operações logísticas, a adoção de baterias e sistemas BESS representa um divisor de águas. A tecnologia deixa de ser apenas uma alternativa ecológica e passa a funcionar como um seguro operacional estratégico. Ao blindar propriedades e indústrias contra oscilações e quedas de energia na rede de distribuição tradicional, o armazenamento garante previsibilidade, corte de custos operacionais e máxima eficiência para o motor econômico do estado. A redação do portal CenárioMT esclarece aos seus leitores que os dados estatísticos referentes ao crescimento das buscas nacionais por soluções de armazenamento de eletricidade — incluindo o avanço expressivo dos sistemas BESS e das baterias estacionárias no Google entre setembro de 2025 e agosto de 2026 — foram oficialmente enviados à nossa equipe de jornalismo pela Descarbonize Soluções, empresa especializada em transição energética e energia solar. Receba em primeira mão nossas notícias, tendências e exclusivas.

artigo.texto: Making Carbon Pay for Ireland’s Energy Transition: What a Modernised Emissions Trading System Could Mean for Ireland’s Energy Supply Could a modernised EU Emissions Trading System help Ireland ensure a more self-reliant and resilient energy supply? In response to rising energy prices and their impact on European industry, the European Commission published a proposal to modernise the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) on the 17 July 2026. Ireland has been severely impacted by the rising cost of energy caused by Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine, and the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East. In addition to sparking public protests, the energy crisis has imposed significant costs on industry, the State, and consumers. With this in mind, this blog will explore how a modernised ETS could support Ireland in its energy transition. What is the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS)? The EU ETS is a European Union (EU)-wide carbon market on which carbon emission allowances, each worth the equivalent of one tonne of carbon dioxide, are exchanged via a cap-and-trade system. Under this system, companies must cover their carbon emissions with allowances that have either been freely allocated to them, that have been auctioned off by Member States, or that have been bought from other companies. This creates an economic incentive for companies to reduce their carbon emissions. Each year, the overall cap on allowances is lowered, in theory, driving a gradual reduction in carbon emissions. The EU ETS is the primary decarbonisation policy of the EU’s Green Deal and has proven to be fairly effective. Since is was launched in 2005, the ETA has helped emissions to be cut by around 50%, and since 2013, it has raised over 270 billion euros in auction revenues. Ireland has taken in 1.28 billion euros through EU ETS allowance auctions since 2013. From the 139 million euros raised in 2024 under the scheme, the vast majority (102.3 million euros) has gone to the Department of Transport and been invested in public transport projects. In addition the EU ETS revenue has also funded specific projects in Ireland through EU-level funds. For example, the ETS revenue funded an EU Innovation Fund grand of 39 million euros to the Saoirse Wave Energy Project located in Ireland. For these EU-level funds, the Irish National Contact Point is the Environment and Climate Research and Advisory Unit in the Department of the Environment, Climate and Communications (DCEE). Ireland’s energy supply vulnerability Recent geopolitical events have exposed one of Ireland’s strategic vulnerabilities as one of the most import-dependent economies in the EU when it comes to energy, with 80% of its energy supply being imported in 2024. This number can be explained by the fact that Ireland continues to rely heavily on fossil fuels. Of Ireland’s 168.0 TWh energy supply in 2024, fossil-fuel made up for 81.3%. Meanwhile, the country as yet does not produce or harvest much energy of its own. Therefore, to minimise the impact of future energy crises and to render Ireland’s energy supply more independent, policymakers should certainly consider how to foster the country's homegrown energy production capacity. For this, a modernised EU ETS, as proposed by the European Commission could be useful. How a modernised EU ETS could support Ireland’s energy transition In response to the ongoing energy crisis, the European Commission was invited by the European Council to draft a proposal for a review of the EU ETS. The aim of this review is to make the EU ETS a more effective instrument to strengthen independence, innovation and competitiveness in Europe. Its guiding idea is to redirect current expenditure on imported fossil fuel towards investments in the green transition. In the proposition published by the European Commission, two elements are particularly relevant to Ireland’s situation. First, the Commission’s proposal includes provisions to reform the Market Stability Reserve (MSR). The MSR was first established in 2018 as, at that time, carbon prices were considered too low to provide companies with a sufficient incentive to reduce their emissions. A mechanism that invalidates the carbon allowances surplus was thus introduced. Today, however, the opposite problem seems to be the case, as excessively high carbon prices are being passed on to electricity prices, thus increasing costs for businesses and consumers. Therefore, the proposal suggests stopping the invalidation of the surplus, and instead, sets it aside as a buffer that could be used if prices rise unexpectedly in the future. In principle, this reform of the MSR should ensure better market stability and reduce price volatility, which should be of interest to Irish policy makers. Second, the Commission’s proposal introduces a number of measures aimed at improving the use of EU ETS revenue. The underlying principle is that EU ETS revenue should go back to industry to support its decarbonisation efforts. If funds to that effect were already in existence, such as the aforementioned Innovation Fund, the proposal aims to establish an Industrial Decarbonisation Bank (IDB) that will enable investment at a bigger scale. The Commission also considers that there should be better control over the way Member States spend their EU ETS revenues. The revenue should be spent on genuine climate action, which, according to the WWF, is not always the case. How could this benefit Ireland? A modernised ETS with an amended MSR could protect the EU, and thus Ireland, from carbon-price volatility in the allowance market, limiting the extent to which fluctuations in allowance prices contribute to electricity costs. In the longer term, clean energy investments, such as those supported by a modernised EU ETS, can help reduce the impacts of energy crises. artigo.texto: Texas residents promised a state-ordered freeze on data center permits are instead watching approvals advance and public comment deadlines tick down. Nearly a month after Gov. Greg Abbott directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to pause issuing permits for data center projects on Sept. 12, the advocacy group said the agency had issued several water-related authorizations and continued reviewing air permit applications. Residents trying to understand what the pause actually stopped were advised by agency’s own staff to treat public comment as active, the group said. Communities struggling to link corporate names to construction sites face mounting confusion as state agencies continue issuing permits despite a promised freeze. That confusion plagues residents near Lufkin, where investigative reporting previously uncovered a web of separate corporate entities handling the proposed Amp Z development's air permits, land deals and political backing. The newspaper later found that a TCEQ reviewer asked whether the proposed power plant’s emissions could be lowered enough to avoid a more extensive federal pollution review, further minimizing’s the areas where residents can voice concerns. “The TCEQ’s own data indicates that it’s business as usual for data centers,” said Kathryn Guerra, director of Public Citizen’s TCEQ Watchdog Campaign. “Affected communities were promised a freeze. Instead, they’re getting another reason to distrust the TCEQ and ineffective attempts to govern by press release.” Public Citizen released its findings the same day the TCEQ was due to update Abbott’s office on its compliance with his directive. When the governor announced the pause through a late September directive, he formally called for state reviews of data centers before making permitting decisions. “Until they do, TCEQ will issue no permits sought by data center projects,” Abbott said in the announcement. Public Citizen identified 16 permit actions that came after Abbott’s directive, including seven new construction stormwater authorizations, one amended stormwater authorization and an industrial wastewater permit renewal. Stormwater authorizations were cited as examples of approvals that were issued after Abbott’s announcements by Guerra. Those authorizations allow stormwater discharges from construction sites. Public Citizen identified seven counties, with approvals dated from Sept. 22 through Oct. 13. Following the nonprofit’s investigation, Guerra said Public Citizen has not yet approached the governor’s office about its findings, which it began compiling late last week. Abbott’s directive followed months of pressure over the industry’s demands on electricity, water and rural communities. Some Republican leaders even crossed party lines, such as Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller, who called for a temporary moratorium on new hyperscale data center developments, arguing that Texas needed to assess the effects on infrastructure and agriculture before the state could allow the rapid expansion to continue. Notably, Abbott’s September audit of data centers seeking to connect to the electric grid and subsequent pause on environmental permits has not accounted for facilities that plan to generate their own electricity, allowing them to proceed without relying on the grid-connection, The Texas Tribune reported. A separate Tribune analysis published Monday found Abbott had received about $9 million since July 2025 from donors with direct or indirect ties to data centers, representing about 13% of his fundraising during that period. Abbott’s campaign spokesman Eduardo Leal defended the governor’s position to the Tribune, saying his priorities remained on protecting the grid, requiring data centers to cover their costs and preventing disruption to communities. But for people living near the proposed facilities, the immediate concern is whether the promise of a pause could cause them to miss their opportunity to respond and voice their opinion. Public Citizen said the TCEQ mailed notices Sept. 22 for three major source air permit applications involving power facilities near Abilene and in Hill County. The notice for the Nexus project in Hubbard has a public comment deadline of Friday, Oct. 23, according to the group’s review. Guerra said a senior agency staff member told Public Citizen that residents should treat the deadline as active. Public Citizen asked commissioners Oct. 7 to clarify the situation or withdraw the notices, she said. Without state clarification on whether public comment periods remain active, residents are left scrambling to meet deadlines while navigating contradictory signals from Austin. The group also argued that people are being asked to comment on permit applications without truly knowing or being able to access the findings of the state’s review. When asked whether the Sept. 22 mailing dates could have simply been a reflection of notices that may have been prepared before the directive, Guerra acknowledged that possibility. But she said subsequent steps in the public participation portion have only continued. For Linda Polley of Save Hill County, residents also are still seeing work continue on the ground. Trucks traveling the roads with loads, cranes working, large piles of dirt and walls going up are what can be found at the Nexus construction site. Polley said nighttime lighting is visible even from her home 15 miles away. “What exactly did you pause?” Polley asked about Abbott, urging the governor to explain what communities should expect as the state’s review proceeds. In Caldwell County, resident Claudia Hollern said neighbors began examining and monitoring permits as they learned that proposed data centers would rely on large power-generating facilities to be built nearby. She described residents trying to follow applications filed under company names they did not initially recognize which had residents following one piece of infrastructure which led to another. artigo.texto: At Humber's Barrett Centre for Technology Innovation (Barrett CTI), a new mobile Electric Vehicle (EV) Battery Assembly System is giving students hands-on experience in a rapidly growing industry, equipping them with the skills and knowledge to work with the technologies that are shaping the future of automotive manufacturing. The new system was made possible through a donation from the RBC Foundation and showcased on October 15, 2026, at the Barrett CTI. Designed specifically to replicate real-world EV battery assembly, students work with two KUKA industrial robots as they move components from storage onto a shuttle. A magnetic planar table transports the shuttle through simulated battery-production stations, where technologies such as 2D and 3D vision systems, robotic grippers and tool changers demonstrate how modern manufacturing comes together. The robots ultimately complete the simulated battery module and return it to storage. "This system represents much more than new equipment. It creates exciting opportunities to prepare our students for careers in the rapidly growing clean energy, electric vehicle, and advanced manufacturing sectors," said Neal Mohammed, director, Barrett CTI. "Our vision is to build on this foundation by integrating emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and condition monitoring. These advancements will strengthen our training capabilities, support innovation, and help our industry partners develop the skilled workforce they need to remain competitive." The greatest advantage for students is the opportunity to learn across disciplines. The Battery Assembly System brings together robotics, automation, electronics, programming, mechanical engineering, systems integration and quality control into one working environment. Rather than learning individual technologies in isolation, students we will be focusing on the system as part of the curriculum for Humber's Mechatronics degree program and Electromechanical Engineering Technology program and develop the problem-solving skills needed to understand how an entire automated system works, and how to troubleshoot it when something goes wrong. That multidisciplinary approach is already making an impact. Humber students, such as Tete Soto, saw the Battery Assembly System in action by working alongside Barrett CTI technologists. In their third year of Humber's Electromechanical Engineering Technology program, Soto is excited that the Battery Assembly System is being integrated into their learning: "Now we have an idea of how it all comes together. [The Battery Assembly System] is lighting the way for students to learn how to make fully functioning robotic systems." As the system is larger than any capstone project, the learning opportunity will train students to be better prepared for jobs in various engineering fields. Humber students have also been trained to lead STEAM workshops, introducing visiting middle and high school students to the technologies found in the Battery Assembly System. More than 1,200 middle and high school students have encountered the system through tours of the Barrett CTI. RBC Foundation's support of the Battery Assembly System also allows Humber to connect directly with industry. Organizations such as KUKA Robotics, Rockwell Automation, SICK Sensor Intelligence, DMG Mori, Javelin, Pilz, B&R and Weidmuller have contributed their technology, expertise or support and approximately 56 industry and government visitors have already seen the Battery Assembly System during its build phase. The Battery Assembly System is mobile, ensuring its impact can extend beyond the classrooms at Humber. It can be brought into high-traffic spaces for demonstrations, workshops and tours, making advanced EV manufacturing available and accessible. Recently, the Battery Assembly System was showcased at the PAC Global Disruptors Summit in June 2026. "RBC Foundation is committed to fostering innovation and sustainability and is proud to support Humber's Barrett Centre for Technology Innovation with an $800,000 contribution," says Chris Misch, regional vice-president, Toronto Downtown, RBC. "This funding will help advance the mobile Electric Vehicle (EV) Battery Assembly System, a transformative initiative that equips students with hands-on skills in automation, robotics, and clean-energy technologies." "Aligned with RBC's sustainability goals and Humber's leadership in applied learning, the collaboration will help to strengthen Ontario's position in the green economy while empowering the next generation of innovators. Together, we are helping build ecosystems where education, industry, and communities thrive, supporting the progress towards a brighter, more sustainable future for all."

artigo.texto: Both incumbent Rep. Eugene Vindman and Douglas Ollivant, his Republican challenger, say they want to put the brakes on data centers in sensitive areas but have different ideas about how to provide relief to people feeling the sting of higher prices. Vindman, 51, is a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel and former legal adviser for the National Security Council. Ollivant, 58, is also a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel and served as the director for Iraq on the National Security Council. He was recently diagnosed with an aggressive form of leukemia but chose to stay in the race. The 7th Congressional District includes parts of Prince William, Stafford, Spotsylvania, Culpeper, King George, Madison, Orange, Greene and Albemarle counties and the city of Fredericksburg. U.S. Rep. Eugene Vindman, D-7th, and his Republican challenger, Douglas Ollivant, submitted … The Prince William Times asked both candidates to weigh in on three issues ahead of the Nov. 3 election. The economy and rising prices Economic issues, including rising prices for everyday goods and fuel, are the top issue for voters going into this year's midterms, according to several recent surveys. Vindman said lowering costs has been “a top priority” for his office. He said he supports legislation to lower utility bills, provide relief from high diesel prices and lower healthcare prescription costs for military families. “Everywhere I go in Virginia's Seventh District, I hear the same thing: families are struggling to keep up with the rising cost of living. Whether it's filling up their gas tanks, putting groceries on the table, paying their utility bills, or affording health care, hardworking Virginians are being stretched to the breaking point,” Vindman said. Vindman also said he is committed to repealing Republicans’ “Big Beautiful Bill,” which slashed Medicaid funding and raised health-care premiums for people insured under the Affordable Care Act. Ollivant, however, said politicians need to be “more forthright” with the public about how government decisions impact kitchen table issues. “Politicians need to quit treating the public as infants and start leveling with us as adults. Prices are higher and are going to stay that way until the economy recovers and there is broader stability overseas — including Ukraine and Iran,” Ollivant said. Immigration enforcement The 7th District has one of the highest immigrant populations in the state, with 16% of residents having moved there from another country. The Prince William Times asked both candidates whether they support the Trump administration’s immigration policies andwhat should be done differently. Ollivant did not directly criticize President Trump’s approach. He said the country’s immigration laws need to be enforced and questioned adopting any policy that would “allow violent illegal immigrants to prey upon our communities.” He also said immigration officers should be treated better by opponents of the president’s agenda. “Few people put their lives on the line in the same way they do, enforcing our laws and keeping our families safe. They deserve a lot better than the broad brush applied by their detractors,” he said. Vindman, who immigrated to the U.S. from Ukraine as a child, said he opposes the Trump administration’s enforcement tactics. “Americans deserve an immigration system that keeps our communities safe, upholds the rule of law, and respects the dignity and rights of every person,” Vindman said. “As a former prosecutor and 25-year Army veteran, I know we can and must secure our borders without abandoning our values or treating our neighbors with cruelty.” Vindman said he would support reforms to immigration enforcement, such as requiring ICE officers to remove their masks, wear body cameras, issue judicial warrants, and ensure clear constitutional protections. He’d also like the agency to adopt enforceable use-of-force standards and conduct independent investigations when federal agents are accused of breaking the law. “As an immigrant whose family came to this country seeking freedom and opportunity, I believe deeply in the promise of America,” Vindman said. Data centers and electricity The rapid proliferation of data centers has provoked widespread backlash among Northern Virginia residents. It has also caused concerns about how those data centers will get their electrical power. New transmission line corridors and electrical substations have been proposed, some of which will be near homes, schools and businesses. Vindman said he is concerned about data centers being placed near sensitive areas, such as neighborhoods, schools and parks, but stopped short of calling for a moratorium. “Data centers should not be built near national parks, schools, or residential communities, and Virginians should not be stuck paying higher utility bills to support their growth. I firmly believe rural communities should not be forced to shoulder the costs and consequences of transmission infrastructure built to benefit everyone else,” he said. Vindman added that he is “deeply concerned” about the rapid expansion of transmission lines being built to serve data centers. “Hardworking Virginians should not be forced to pay higher utility bills, lose their land, or watch their communities transformed just so billion-dollar technology companies can turn a bigger profit,” he said. Ollivant said he is against data center development on farmland and on battlefields but did not respond to questions about whether he would support slowing data center development.The electrical grid in Virginia needs to be upgraded, Ollivant said, and he would consider “smart solutions” to boost the grid. “We can do a lot of good with advances in technology and economic growth in Virginia. We can't solve any of these problems, much less pay for basic services, without economic growth and technological innovation,” Ollivant said. Unveiled at Equip Expo 2026, the lineup includes the next-generation ALLPRO battery technology and AP series of tools; SFA 120 snow thrower, STIHL's first-ever snow thrower; the AZ Mower Series, the company's first gas-powered stand-on zero-turn mowers; HEXA™ technology chainsaw chain that stays sharp 50% longer than a full-chisel chain, and new value-priced homeowner battery-powered equipment and combo kits. Together, the introductions are designed to help professionals be more productive with less downtime across seasons and give homeowners a simpler approach to yard care. "As we enter our second century, our focus remains on solving the challenges our customers face every day," said Ricky Cacchiotti, vice president of product management at STIHL Inc. "That means helping professional crews stay productive across demanding jobs and giving homeowners dependable tools that make caring for their property easier." More Ways to Work Across the Seasons The new SFA 120 battery-powered snow thrower marks STIHL's entry into snow removal, giving property owners another way to put their battery equipment to work throughout the year. Its 22-inch clearing width, 180-degree adjustable chute, rubber auger system, and a snow-throwing distance of up to 30 feet provide controlled clearing on driveways and other paved surfaces. When paired with the new ALLPRO AP 300.0 P battery, which features a cold-start function, the tool is ready for use in outdoor temperatures as low as -4°F. More Mowing Options from STIHL As landscaping professionals prepare for another busy growing season, STIHL is expanding its zero-turn mower lineup with the new AZ Series, its first gas-powered stand-on model. Powered by Kawasaki® engines and dual Hydro-Gear® drives, the series reaches speeds up to 9 mph, while a 7-gauge welded steel deck and reinforced frame stand up to daily professional use. An adjustable suspension platform padded thigh support, no-flat front tires and large rear tires help support operator comfort, stability and control across a variety of mowing conditions. The new stand-on models join the STIHL RZ Professional 400 Series and RZ Professional 500 Series, giving crews more options to match their equipment to the property and job. Available with 54- or 60-inch mower decks, the ride-on zero-turn mowers pair rugged welded steel frames, fabricated decks and proven Kawasaki® engines with patented front and rear suspension designed to absorb impacts, maintain ground contact and reduce operator fatigue. With forward speeds up to 9 mph, the expanded lineup is built to keep commercial crews moving efficiently throughout the growing season. The AP 300.0 P battery delivers up to 60% higher peak power and 20% longer runtime than the previous-generation AP 300.0 S. It joins a portfolio built for a range of professional applications, including the MSA 240 T for in-tree work, the MSA 300 and MSA 600 for day-to-day tree care, and the MS 400.1 for demanding felling. The new HEXA™ cutting system further helps professionals stay productive, offering up to 50% longer edge retention compared to a full-chisel chain and up to 20% more cuts per charge or tank than a semi-chisel chain, with easier sharpening in the field. The lineup also introduces the first STIHL combo kit, packaging the FSA 60 R trimmer, BGA 50 blower, battery, and charger together. artigo.texto: Agility Robotics, a humanoid robotics and physical AI company, has announced that Nyobolt, a pioneer of high-power, ultra-fast charging solutions, is the technology provider to Agility. The technology powers one of Digit 5’s most significant upgrades: a fast recharge battery system that enables Digit to work more than 20 hours in a 24-hour day. Agility recently unveiled Digit 5 as its first humanoid robot designed for cooperatively safe work at scale, allowing it to work in close proximity to people. As part of its upgrades, Digit 5 will feature a new battery system that delivers 90-minutes of runtime and charges in just 9 minutes, achieving a 10:1 run-to-charge ratio, up from Digit 4’s 2:1 ratio. This rapid charge capability is designed to keep Digit working, enabling more than two shifts in a single day and helping customers get more from each robot. Daniel Diez, chief business officer of Agility Robotics, says: “For our customers, Digit’s uptime is the business case. Digit 5 will deliver more than 20 hours of productive work in a 24-hour day, more than two full shifts. “That’s the kind of gain that materially improves the value customers get from Digit and the economics of deploying a humanoid robot fleet. Nyobolt’s ultra-fast charging technology gets us there, and it’s one of the pieces that makes Digit 5 ready for full-scale operation.” Nyobolt’s unique high-power battery technology is built for demanding industrial conditions, combining fast charging, exceptional cycle life, and reduced system weight. By removing the power bottleneck that has historically constrained autonomous robot fleet economics, the system addresses a key constraint on robot utilization: downtime. The result is a compelling potential advantage for Digit 5 customers, who can target longer operating windows, more productive shifts and more demanding task sequences. Combined with Agility’s experience deploying humanoid robots in real commercial environments, this battery performance is designed to strengthen Digit’s value proposition for warehouse, distribution and manufacturing operations. Sai Shivareddy, co-founder and CEO at Nyobolt, says: “Nyobolt’s technology was chosen because Digit 5 will need more power from a smaller, lighter pack, in environments where reliability isn’t optional. “Agility set an exceptionally high bar for what a battery has to withstand in live warehouse and manufacturing environments, and this partnership shows what’s possible when ultra-fast charging is engineered for the toughest conditions in physical AI.” Early access to Digit 5 equipped with Nyobolt’s battery technology is expected to begin in the first half of 2027, with increasing availability over the following six to nine months for manufacturing, warehouse and distribution operators. Agility is preparing to become a public company through its previously announced business combination with Churchill Capital Corp XI. The business combination is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, after which the combined company will operate as Agility Robotics and is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “AGLT”.

artigo.texto: Huawei has stepped into the battery swapping track, joining hands with CATL to promote the energy replenishment for autonomous driving. From this very moment, the battery swapping track may truly take off at an unprecedented speed: The leading smart tech player Huawei and the top battery manufacturer CATL are joining forces to develop battery swapping services! The two sides have carried out cooperation before, and Huawei is not the only user of CATL's battery swapping service, but this collaboration is far from ordinary: It comes with an unprecedented technical chain, innovative and distinctive product solutions, and almost no restrictions on implementation scope... The combination of these elements is a signal that will subvert traditional business models. What exactly are Huawei and CATL going to do this time? First, let's sort out the division of responsibilities of all parties involved. The entities signing this agreement include Huawei's Zhiyuan Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., CATL, and its battery swapping business-related entity EVOGO. Generally, Zhiyuan provides intelligent vehicle solutions, CATL provides battery technology and its chocolate battery swapping system, while EVOGO participates in the construction of battery swapping networks and related operation services. The goal put forward by the three parties is to promote Huawei Qiankun cooperative models to access CATL's chocolate battery swapping network, and realize the interconnection of the vehicle end, station end and cloud end. This means that the cooperation is not just adding several battery swapping station locations to the vehicle navigation system, nor is it just equipping a single car model with a swappable battery. The three parties aim to build a set of collaborative mechanism covering from vehicle demand to station service: when the vehicle needs energy replenishment, the system can plan a suitable battery swapping station; after arriving at the station, the vehicle can connect with the battery swapping equipment; after the battery swapping is completed, the vehicle can resume its normal trip. The 99-second battery swapping index announced by CATL corresponds to the battery replacement process alone. This cannot be directly equated with the total time from when the vehicle decides to replenish energy to when it drives away from the battery swapping station, let alone conclude that the entire set of unmanned battery swapping services has been realized solely based on this single index. What is really worth analyzing is how the intelligent driving system and the battery swapping station cooperate with each other. After all, there are still many technical details to be solved between the scenario that a vehicle can complete navigation and driving on open roads and the scenario that it can accurately drive into a specific workstation and park at the exact position required by the equipment. From self-searching for stations to automatic battery swapping, how to get through the technical chain? If we split the whole process apart, the first step actually happens on the vehicle side. First, the vehicle needs to judge whether energy replenishment is needed by combining its battery status, remaining driving range and travel plan. This capability can be provided by Huawei's on-board model, on the premise that the car manufacturer grants Huawei sufficiently high underlying permissions; of course, it can also be independently developed by the car manufacturer itself. If the user chooses battery swapping, the system will also comprehensively consider the location of stations, supported vehicle models and actual availability to determine which station to go to. Next, the vehicle needs to switch from road driving mode to station operation mode, which is the core value of Huawei in this cooperation. On open roads, the assisted driving system mainly deals with road structures, traffic participants, driving routes and dynamic obstacles and other issues. But after entering the battery swapping station, the environment and tasks will change: the entrance may be narrow, the internal passages and parking spaces in the station have clear restrictions, and the vehicle must finally park at the precise position where the battery swapping equipment can work normally. This puts forward higher requirements for the vehicle's positioning, environmental perception and low-speed control performance: Navigation that brings the vehicle near the station is only the first half of the whole process; the vehicle also needs to identify the entrance, understand the internal passage route of the station, and complete the parking alignment according to the requirements of the battery swapping workstation. Of course, the current ADS 5 version can easily handle scenarios such as passing through gates and toll stations, and it can also handle narrow and complex parking spaces with great ease. The only thing to do is to collect enough scenario data of CATL's battery swapping stations to ensure 100% reliability. After the vehicle is parked stably, the battery swapping equipment takes over the work, which is the home field of CATL. CATL's standard battery swapping station is compatible with vehicles with a wheelbase ranging from 2.55 meters to 3.1 meters. Each standard battery swapping station is equipped with 14 to 30 battery compartments, with a 99.99% battery swapping success rate and a 99-second swapping duration. In actual operation, the battery swapping process for users is as convenient as refueling, but the cost is greatly reduced. After the battery swapping is completed, the whole process is not over. The vehicle needs to confirm the battery status, safely drive away from the workstation, and reconnect to the navigation and driving tasks. Only when all the links before and after are connected, can users get a continuous experience from the road to the station, and then from the station back to the road. artigo.texto: 15GWh Energy Storage, 30 Billion kWh Transactions: Huanghe Digital Energy Raises Tens of Millions of Yuan in Pre-A Round Financing, the Most Costly Link in the Energy Storage Sector Has Finally Been Separately Priced Energy Insight learned that Huanghe Digital Energy recently completed a Pre-A round of financing of tens of millions of yuan, jointly led by the North China Electric Power University Education Foundation and a leading enterprise in the energy storage industry chain. The use of funds is very clear: the engineering implementation of the vertical power industry model, the large-scale replication of energy storage asset operation capabilities, and the expansion of the R&D team. In the same period, as the only new-type market participant in the power sector, Huanghe Digital Energy was invited to join the "Education Community" jointly established by North China Electric Power University and State Grid. This seems to reflect that in the era when AI is reshaping all industries, power, as the "life source" of AI, is also in urgent need of compound talents who understand the market, power and AI. The field that this company is deeply engaged in provides a fertile test ground for universities and the power grid side. The company's model is quite unique — as an investor that holds energy storage power stations by itself, it also entrusts the operation of multiple third-party power stations. Up to now, its total accumulated operation scale has exceeded 15GWh, and the total accumulated traded electricity volume has exceeded 30 billion kWh. Objectively speaking, this financing scale is not prominent in the current energy storage track, but the direction it bets on is worth examining: when the revenue of energy storage power stations increasingly depends on who makes the "charge and discharge" decisions for them, whether the operation capability itself can be separated from specific people and specific provinces and precipitated into a set of standardized capabilities that can be delivered in batches, is becoming a key variable that determines the industry pattern. 01 Operators of energy storage power stations are becoming a variable in the asset pricing chain The asset attribute of energy storage power stations has undergone an easily overlooked change in 2026. In February 2025, Document No.136 promoted the full access of grid-connected new energy power to the market; in January 2026, Document No.114 included independent energy storage into the capacity tariff mechanism. After the rules are unified, national power assets begin to face the same set of price signals, and the decision-making power of revenue shifts from "generating more power" to "selling power at better prices". On April 28, 2026, the "Caitong Asset Management - Canadian Solar Held Real Estate Asset-backed Special Plan (Carbon Neutrality)" was established, becoming the first inter-institutional REITs with energy storage power stations as the underlying assets in China, and was listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in June. In August, the 304 million yuan energy storage REITs project of Huanghe Tianwei was accepted by the Shanghai Stock Exchange. What REITs value is predictable cash flow, and whether the cash flow of energy storage power stations can be predicted depends on operation. This is not an inference, but a question that financial institutions must answer during due diligence. However, an energy storage power station is by no means a machine that automatically generates revenue. China Post Securities has made a set of calculations based on a 100MW/200MWh system: under the assumptions of EPC at 1.6 yuan/Wh, cells at 0.5 yuan/Wh, and 260 days of operation per year, the after-tax IRR of independent energy storage in Shanxi is 5.9%, and that in Shandong is -1.8%. The source of the gap is not the battery, but the revenue structure. The revenue in Shanxi includes primary frequency regulation, contributing about 63,000 yuan per day on average; the benchmark spot price spread assumption in Shandong is only 0.4 yuan/kWh, 0.1 yuan lower than that in Shanxi, and the capacity compensation is limited. With the same set of equipment, crossing a provincial boundary, the account book is completely different. This is why operation is pushed to the forefront. Asset holders can be industrial capital, financial institutions, and local state-owned enterprises, but making a power station complete every declaration, every charge and discharge without errors in the rules of its own province is becoming a matter that requires special capabilities. The particularity of energy storage power stations is that they play two roles at the same time: they are power sources when discharging, and loads when charging. The revenue needs to be superimposed from three directions: capacity tariff, spot arbitrage and auxiliary services, and the weight of each layer varies from province to province and continues to drift — wind power and photovoltaic only need to manage the source side, while energy storage needs to put role switching, market declaration and battery boundaries into the same decision-making, which is the new energy asset with the longest decision chain among the three types. Hengyi Group entrusted Xinghe Microgrid with the full life-cycle operation of its 113.5MW/226.72MWh energy storage power station cluster, and the contract covers real-time monitoring, fault response and power trading assistance. The bid price for the operation and maintenance service of the 200MW/400MWh shared energy storage power station of Jiyang Green Energy Storage is 48 million yuan (including tax). Guoneng Rixin provides full trusteeship service of power trading for a 100MW/400MWh energy storage power station in Yongning County, Ningxia, with a trusteeship fee of 1.5 million yuan per year.
