artigo.texto: Is NIO no longer alone? Huawei teams up with CATL to launch battery swapping services: diversified energy replenishment is the trend. A few days ago, Huawei Yinwang Intelligent signed a cooperation agreement with CATL and CATL Digital Energy to jointly build an open intelligent battery swapping system. Shortly afterwards, media outlets including LatePost Auto, CLSA, and Blue Whale Auto successively disclosed that the first batch of Yinwang's battery swapping models is tentatively set to five, which are planned to be launched in 2027. The first model will be under the Yijing brand co-developed by Dongfeng and Huawei, and Qijing, the brand jointly built by GAC and Huawei, has also arranged battery swapping models. Earlier this year, BYD launched its super flash charging technology and the second-generation Blade Battery, which is claimed to "fully charge in 5 minutes, reach full capacity in 9 minutes, and only take 3 more minutes at -30°C". In April, CATL launched its third-generation Shenxing Super Charging Battery at its Super Science Day, with a peak charging rate of 15C and an equivalent 10C, which can be fully charged in 6 minutes at normal temperature. Against the backdrop that the time gap between energy replenishment via charging and battery swapping is getting smaller and smaller, and fast charging stations are becoming increasingly popular, Huawei Yinwang has chosen to join the battery swapping model, probably because it has seen the deeper value of the battery swapping model. Battery swapping is far more than just an energy replenishment solution Speaking of battery swapping, NIO is the first car brand that most people will think of. On October 19, NIO officially announced that the number of its battery swapping stations has reached 4186. During the National Day holiday this year, NIO's charging and swapping facilities provided more than 2 million services in total. For users of battery swapping models, battery swapping is not only an energy replenishment solution, but also a more convenient, stable, and even "unnoticeable" energy replenishment experience. Yinwang Intelligent follows the same logic. Huawei's Qiankun Intelligent Driving and CATL's Choco-Swap network carry out in-depth collaborative scheduling, and connect the vehicle end, station end and cloud end systems, so that the vehicle can independently determine the energy replenishment demand according to the real-time battery status and users' travel habits, realizing a full closed-loop process of independently finding stations, driving into stations, automatically aligning, completing 99-second fully automatic battery swapping, and driving away on its own. (Source: Photo by Dianchetong) In the past, under the battery swapping model, users could quickly complete energy replenishment without getting off the vehicle. Now, users do not even need to consider the energy replenishment of their vehicles at all, as the system can handle everything. This sci-fi-like scenario has become a reality. In contrast, at charging stations, users still need to manually open the charging port and insert the charging gun, which has not completely got rid of the demand for manual operation. In addition, battery swapping remains a shortcut to achieve differentiated competition. NIO has reached cooperation on the battery swapping model with many automakers including Changan, Geely, JAC, Chery, FAW and GAC. However, up to now, other automakers have not launched models adapted to NIO's battery swapping stations, and most non-NIO battery swapping models are commercial vehicles. The number of household cars that support battery swapping is relatively small, and NIO is the only player in the high-end market. The two brands Yijing and Qijing, which are cooperatively developed by Huawei Yinwang, Dongfeng and GAC, can quickly achieve differentiated competition by matching the battery swapping model with Qiankun Intelligent Driving. (Source: Photo by Dianchetong) More importantly, at the recent performance meeting, CATL stated that more than 2500 Choco-Swap stations for passenger vehicles have been built, covering 200 cities across China, and the number will increase to 3000 by the end of the year. Unconsciously, the scale of CATL's battery swapping stations has been large enough to meet users' daily energy replenishment needs. CATL is different from NIO. NIO is an automaker, and its battery swapping ecosystem is relatively closed. Although it is moving towards openness, there are still many restrictions, so many automakers are unwilling to join NIO's battery swapping ecosystem. CATL is a battery manufacturer, and Choco-Swap is built on an open attitude. In addition to CATL building battery swapping stations itself, other enterprises can also independently build battery swapping stations based on CATL's standardized battery modules and construction standards. This cooperation model can rapidly expand the coverage of battery swapping stations after being recognized by partners. Perhaps it is precisely because the battery swapping model has inherent advantages in energy replenishment and differentiated competition, coupled with the huge battery swapping ecosystem that CATL has built to meet the energy replenishment needs of users of Yijing and Qijing battery swapping models, that Huawei has firmly chosen to join the battery swapping ecosystem even when the charging speed is getting faster and faster. It is never too late to join the marathon of battery swapping It is undeniable that with the current increasingly fast charging speed, the advantages of battery swapping are shrinking, but considering the carrying capacity of the power grid, it is almost impossible for charging to be faster than battery swapping. The more stable and faster battery swapping will always have its value to exist. In 2018, NIO's first battery swapping station was put into operation in Nanshan Science and Technology Park, Shenzhen. artigo.texto: In 2027, Chinese manufacturers only won half of the Dutch residential energy storage market. On September 23, Sungrow announced that its latest all-in-one residential energy storage system, PowerHarbor, has been officially launched for sale in Europe, with the Netherlands selected as its first stop. Product image of PowerHarbor. Image source: Sungrow Why the Netherlands, instead of familiar major residential storage markets like Germany? Because in just over two months, Dutch households will "have no choice but to buy home batteries". Around 3 million households in the Netherlands have installed solar panels on their rooftops. For more than two decades, they have been enjoying a favorable policy: Excess electricity generated during the day is fed into the grid; when there is a shortage of power at night, they draw electricity back from the grid. They can store as much as they take out, with almost no handling fees charged. The grid acts like a free power bank. On January 1, 2027, this free power bank will be taken away. Going forward, for each kilowatt-hour of electricity fed into the grid during the day, the law only guarantees a return of just over 40 euro cents; but buying one kilowatt-hour of electricity at night costs around 1.9 euros. After deducting various fees charged by power companies, the electricity fed to the grid by many households is almost given away for free. The most cost-effective solution is to install a residential storage battery at home: store the excess electricity during the day for self-use at night. Therefore, Dutch research institute Dutch New Energy Research forecasts that the new installed capacity of residential energy storage in the country will skyrocket from 0.86 GWh in 2025 to 4.5 GWh in 2027. A 5.2-fold increase in just two years. By that time, based on the average price of around 470 euros/kWh for residential batteries in the Netherlands in 2025, the 4.5 GWh of new capacity in 2027 corresponds to a hardware market of approximately 2.1 billion euros, or 160 billion RMB. This scale ranks third in Europe, only smaller than that of Germany and Italy. Chinese manufacturers have already taken the lead in this business. According to information from New Energy Industrialist, the two best-selling residential storage brands in the Netherlands at present, Votai and Sungrow Power Supply's residential storage brand Sinexcel, are both from China. Now, Sungrow is also entering the market. But when these Chinese-made batteries are actually installed in the basements of Dutch households, a deeper business reality emerges: the delivery of hardware is only the beginning. When to charge the battery, when to discharge it, and who to sell the excess electricity to at a high price — these issues that determine profit margins are not decided by Chinese manufacturers. The right to set these rules is held by local Dutch power companies. For example, an enterprise called Frank Energie does not manufacture a single battery itself, but it remotely manages more than 14,000 household batteries made by other manufacturers on the cloud every day. This is a bit like Didi: it does not manufacture a single car, but decides where the car goes and how much to charge for each order. Selling batteries is certainly profitable, but it is a highly competitive one-off transaction; those who hold the scheduling rights earn a steady stream of "toll fees" over time. In the feast of European energy transition, Chinese manufacturers, with their exceptional manufacturing capabilities, have won the first half of the "hardware selling" game. But the truly lucrative, compound-return second half of the energy storage business, as well as the other half of the large profits, are still firmly in the hands of those who send electricity bills to Dutch households every month. 01 In 2027, why do people have to buy batteries By the end of 2024, around 3 million households in the Netherlands had installed photovoltaic systems. For more than two decades, almost none of these households needed batteries. The reason is a policy implemented in 2004 called net metering. Excess electricity generated during the day is fed into the grid, which can be offset 1:1 when the household uses electricity. The grid is equivalent to a free power bank, where users can store as much as they take out without paying any handling fees. This "power bank" can no longer sustain the operation. There are too many photovoltaic systems installed, and at noon in summer, there is so much excess electricity that there is nowhere to send it. In June 2025, the Dutch wholesale electricity price dropped below zero for 127 hours, which means that power generators had to pay others to take their electricity, and still could not sell it. But power companies still have to record accounts for photovoltaic users at a retail price of more than 1 euro per kWh. Part of this loss-making business is ultimately passed on to neighbors who have not installed photovoltaic systems. Before the legislation was finalized, power companies took action first. Since the end of 2023, they have successively charged a "feed-in feedback fee" to photovoltaic users: the more electricity users send to the grid, the more fees they have to pay. According to a three-year fixed contract from a large power company in December 2025, if a household sends 2400 kWh of electricity to the grid every year, it has to pay more than 400 euros in feedback fees alone, equivalent to more than 3000 RMB. Users even have to pay extra to send electricity to the grid, and Dutch photovoltaic users have experienced the cost of doing good deeds in advance. The government also wants to reform the policy, but the process has been full of twists and turns. The gradual phase-out plan was rejected by the upper house of parliament in February 2024. artigo.texto: Pilot production system underway Commercialization targeted for late next year SK Nexilis, the copper foil unit backed by SKC's secondary battery investment arm, announced Tuesday it has successfully developed "high-adhesion carbon-coated copper foil" technology, a key material for next-generation batteries. The technology applies a specialized carbon coating to the surface of copper foil to suppress the volumetric expansion of silicon anode materials, improving electrode stability. It addresses a growing industry trend of increasing silicon content in anodes to boost energy density — a shift that makes maintaining strong adhesion between the anode material and the copper foil increasingly critical. The newly developed copper foil is also compatible with dry electrode processing, a next-generation battery manufacturing method drawing growing attention in the industry. SKC expects strong demand from that segment as well, given that adhesion between electrode materials and copper foil is equally critical in dry-process applications. To prepare for full-scale mass production, SK Nexilis is building a pilot production system for the high-adhesion carbon-coated copper foil. The company is currently verifying process stability and plans to secure the technology needed for mass production, targeting commercialization in the second half of 2027. "The development of this high-adhesion carbon-coated copper foil is a result of our efforts to respond to technological shifts in the next-generation battery market — including the expansion of high-silicon-content anode materials and the introduction of dry electrode processing," a company official said. "We will proceed with commercialization optimization without delay, while continuing to develop new technologies to strengthen our competitiveness in the next-generation battery materials market." klee@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: Shares in China's Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL) plunge 12% amid concerns over EV battery demand - Input - 2026-10-21 18:51:47 - Updated - 2026-10-21 18:51:47 [Financial News] Shares in Chinese EV battery maker CATL plunged 12% on the 21st, taking them to around half their May peak. The company's third-quarter results, announced the previous day, fell far short of market expectations. CATL shares listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in China closed at 227.9 yuan, down 12.03% from the previous session. Based on closing prices, that was around half the May 6 peak of 460 yuan, a decline of 50.4%. CATL shares listed in Hong Kong also fell 11.41% that day. CATL said the previous day that its net income for the third quarter rose 14.54% year on year to 21.25 billion yuan (about 4.2 trillion won). That was well below both the second-quarter net income growth rate of 36.5% and the market forecast of 41.2%, compiled by the UK-based London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG). It was also the lowest rate since the fourth quarter of 2024, when it was 13.6%. Third-quarter revenue grew 58.58% year on year to 165.22 billion yuan (about 32.8 trillion won). The growth rate was higher than the 56.9% recorded in the previous quarter, but fell short of the 60.2% market forecast. The Hong Kong-based English-language newspaper South China Morning Post (SCMP) reported that CATL shares have been weak since Chinese EV makers Xiaomi and Li Auto announced last month that they would work with other battery manufacturers. U.S. investment bank JPMorgan said recent tax changes and other factors have caused profitability in China's EV industry to deteriorate faster than expected, potentially affecting demand for CATL's battery products. It also downgraded its investment rating on CATL's Hong Kong-listed shares to “Neutral.” [email protected] Park Jong-won Reporter

artigo.texto: A domestic alternative to Russia’s battery conductive-additive monopoly: Graphene ENG bets on cutting costs - Input - 2026-10-22 16:13:55 - Updated - 2026-10-22 16:13:55 [Financial News] A startup has taken on the challenge of developing a substitute for the “conductive additive,” for which Russia controls at least 95% of global supply. It is Graphene ENG, founded in December 2023. Graphene ENG CEO Lee Jae-young said on the 22nd, “We have developed a technology that uses graphene, a thin sheet, instead of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs), which are shaped like slender tubes, to maintain electrical connections in silicon anode material, and we are on the cusp of commercialization.” Graphite, the main component of pencil lead, consists of thin layers of carbon stacked on top of one another. Graphene is made by peeling away a single layer of carbon atoms. Thin, electrically conductive and flexible, graphene has attracted attention as a material for next-generation electronic devices and batteries. Graphene plays an important role as a conductive additive in batteries. A conductive additive is an ingredient that creates pathways for electricity to flow between the particles that make up an electrode. Only a small amount is used in a battery, but it plays a key role in maintaining electrical connections between particles as the battery repeatedly charges and discharges. This role is especially important in silicon anode material, a next-generation battery material. Anode material stores lithium ions during charging. At the same weight, silicon has about 10 times the theoretical capacity of graphite, which is widely used today. But as it takes in lithium, its volume can swell to as much as four times its original size. Repeated expansion and contraction damage the particles and break electrical connections, reducing battery performance. A leading conductive additive used to address this problem is SWCNTs. Made of carbon, the extremely slender, tube-shaped material connects electrode particles like wires. However, a Russian company has been its exclusive supplier for more than a decade. Lee developed a replacement for SWCNTs using graphene. But to apply it in industrial settings, the company also had to address manufacturing costs and production scale, in addition to performance. Lee saw cost competitiveness as the starting point for expanding the market. “Convinced that the market would open up only once graphene became affordable, I started by changing the manufacturing process,” he explained. Lee, who had been struggling to expand the business, found a way forward through the Korea Industrial Complex Corporation’s “Industrial Complex Open Innovation (KICXUP)” program. Through the program, he was introduced to large companies interested in rechargeable-battery materials. The company is now validating performance with them under real-world application conditions. The next challenge is to reproduce the results achieved in the lab using customers’ materials and manufacturing processes as well. The company is also working to secure intellectual property rights. It has built a technology portfolio that includes one patent registered in the United States and three registered in Korea. Collaboration with customers is also ongoing. Last year, the company signed memorandums of understanding with multiple large companies and began joint proof-of-concept (PoC) testing to develop alternatives to nanomaterials currently sourced from overseas. The experiments are underway. The next step is to expand production. Graphene ENG plans to raise a pre-Series A round this month and set up scale-up equipment by the first half of next year. It aims to reproduce its technology at consistent quality using larger equipment, while also securing supply contracts with customers and certified test reports. In 2028, the company plans to build a large-scale commercial plant backed by Series A funding. Its goal is to increase production, lower the unit price of its products and establish a reliable supply base for customers. “We will prove that domestic technology can produce longer-lasting silicon anodes and carry that effort through to a commercial plant by 2028,” Lee said.Jointly planned by Financial News and the Korea Industrial Complex Corporation[email protected] Kim Hyun-chul Reporter

artigo.texto: Region forging master key for next industrial revolution, proving that whoever can best store electricity holds future of power For a long time, electricity has been a unique energy commodity, with production and consumption happening almost simultaneously. You use it the moment it is generated. But today, as solar and wind power have become China's largest sources of installed capacity, energy storage is quietly building "warehouses" for the power grid. These massive facilities store surplus green electricity during the day and deliver it to factories, shopping malls and millions of households at night. This time-shifting magic has found its grandest stage in North China's Inner Mongolia autonomous region. Driven by the massive deployment of new-type battery facilities designed to support its vast wind and solar power bases, Inner Mongolia has overtaken California to become the world's largest energy storage region. READ MORE: China takes lead in global power storage As of the end of 2025, the region's cumulative installed capacity of new-type energy storage exceeded 25 million kilowatts, ranking first in the nation. Under the blueprint of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), this figure is projected to break the 50 million kW mark, cementing the region's role as the most critical power "reservoir" for the country's renewable mega-bases in the Gobi Desert and other arid areas. The sheer scale of this deployment has triggered a profound industrial metamorphosis. In the past, Inner Mongolia's vast Gobi Desert served merely as an application ground for energy storage, with complete sets of equipment largely purchased from manufacturing clusters in China's eastern provinces. Today, the narrative has shifted from isolated breakthroughs to a multi-city synergy. Hohhot, Baotou and Ordos are firing on all cylinders, forming a differentiated energy storage equipment manufacturing cluster. This has created a new paradigm of "desert application plus multicity collaborative smart manufacturing" — a concentrated reflection of the region's upgrading new energy industry chain. Each city brings a unique strength to the table, but the regional capital, Hohhot, stands out for its specialized focus on system integration and custom solutions engineered for extreme environments. Operating at the forefront of grid resilience, Hohhot's manufacturing sector produces energy storage equipment uniquely designed to withstand the severe cold and punishing sandstorms characteristic of the northern frontiers. While Baotou boasts the most comprehensive industrial chain and Ordos combines equipment manufacturing with ultra-large application scenarios at sites like Envision's zero-carbon industrial park, Hohhot's tailored approach to hostile climate operations ensures these massive systems remain reliable year-round. "Deploying gigawatt-scale battery facilities in the Gobi Desert is fundamentally different from installing systems in temperate coastal plains," said Lin Boqiang, head of the China Institute for Studies in Energy Policy at Xiamen University. "Extreme sub-zero winters can degrade battery performance and discharge efficiency by double digits, while seasonal sandstorms pose severe risks to thermal management and air filtration systems." Hohhot's focus on hostile-climate customization addresses the industry's biggest operational bottleneck — ensuring that massive desert storage parks don't just get built, but actually run safely and reliably 365 days a year, he said. Inner Mongolia's regional triumph mirrors a broader national strategy. Entering 2026, the strategic importance of new-type energy storage has reached unprecedented heights. For the first time, it has been listed among the nation's six emerging pillar industries for the 15th Five-Year Plan. The China New Energy Storage Development Report 2026, released recently by the National Energy Administration, said China's cumulative installed capacity of new-type storage had reached 136 million kW/351 million kilowatt-hours by the end of 2025, representing a year-on-year surge of 84.3 percent. Accounting for roughly 50 percent of the global total, new-type energy storage has surpassed pumped-hydro storage to become China's largest regulating resource, it said. Yet, after years of rapid expansion, the fundamental logic of the industry is evolving. Experts agree that the sector has bid farewell to the era of simple policy-driven scale expansion. "The industry has formally entered a new phase characterized by market-oriented selection, value priority and a focus on quality," said Dai Hongcai, director of the new energy institute at the State Grid Energy Research Institute. While the "forced pairing" of storage with renewable projects drove early growth, future expansion will rely on sustainable business models. The market is also demanding longer duration capabilities. While the average storage duration was around 2.5 hours at the end of 2025, four-hour storage has now become the mainstream, and eight-hour long-duration storage is moving from demonstration to commercial application. This shift ensures that "giant power banks" don't just respond quickly, but can actually sustain the grid through the entire evening peak. As the technology matures, the application boundaries of energy storage are expanding far beyond the traditional power grid. A new and highly lucrative frontier has emerged: the intersection of energy storage and artificial intelligence computing power. In the era of AI large models, a massive global "compute-power race" has sparked acute anxiety over electricity consumption. A single 10,000-GPU computing cluster can consume roughly 100 million kWh of electricity annually. While tech giants in the West are resorting to isolated gas turbines or small nuclear plants to power their AI ambitions, China is leveraging its robust wind, solar and storage ecosystems to pioneer a "compute-power and electricity synergy" model. artigo.texto: CATL Photo: VCG Shares of Chinese battery giant CATL fell more than 10 percent in Shenzhen and Hong Kong stock exchanges on Wednesday, while the company pointed to growth potential in global power and energy-storage battery demand in 2027, supported by rising vehicle electrification and expanding storage markets. CATL's Shenzhen-listed shares were down 12.03 percent at Wednesday's close, while its Hong Kong-listed shares fell 11.413 percent. Results released on Tuesday showed third-quarter revenue rose 58.58 percent year-on-year to a quarterly record of 165.22 billion yuan, while net profit attributable to shareholders increased 14.54 percent to 21.25 billion yuan. But company gross margin fell to 20.69 percent, declining for a second consecutive quarter. At its earnings briefing on Tuesday, CATL attributed the pressure on profitability to changes in its product mix, the resumption of battery consumption tax, and reductions in export tax rebates. The company management said it was discussing how to share the impact with customers while accelerating the introduction of new technologies and products to limit the impact on profitability, the Securities Times reported on Wednesday. And, more tax changes are expected in 2027. The consumption tax, reinstated at 2 percent in September, is set to rise to 4 percent in September 2027. And, battery export VAT rebates were reduced from 9 percent to 6 percent in April and are scheduled to be removed in January 2027. Regarding market demand, however, CATL pointed to more potential opportunities. Responding to investor concerns about 2027, the company cited rising electrification rates and battery capacity per vehicle in China, competitive new electric models in Europe and continued growth in global energy-storage demand. Industry figures showed continued year-on-year growth in both sales and exports. China's combined sales of power and energy storage batteries rose 57.6 percent to 1,681.7 GWh in the first nine months of 2026, while combined exports increased 51.6 percent to 302.9 GWh, according to data released by the China Automotive Battery Innovation Alliance on October 15. In September, combined sales grew 52 percent year-on-year, although they edged down 0.2 percent from August, while exports rose 64.5 percent year-on-year and 3.7 percent month-on-month. "Global demand for power and energy storage batteries may not be as pessimistic as the market expects," CATL management said at the briefing, adding that there was still considerable growth potential. Photo: VCG China has established the world's largest carbon emissions trading market, with cumulative trading volume in its national carbon emissions trading market surpassing one billion tonnes, an official from the Ministry of Ecology and Environment said on Wednesday, highlighting it as one of China's key achievements in tackling climate change. The figures were released at a press conference on Wednesday ahead of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), which will be held in Antalya, Turkey, from November 9 to 20. A Chinese expert said China's sustained efforts in climate action can offer valuable experience for other countries. In just over five years, China has established the world's largest carbon emissions trading market, covering about 8.3 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide, or more than 65 percent of the country's total emissions , said Li Gao, vice minister of ecology and environment, during the press conference held by the State Council Information Office, per Xinhua. In terms of emissions reduction and efficiency gains, China helped reduce carbon dioxide emissions from the thermal power sector by approximately 530 million tonnes during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-25). Internationally, China's carbon market has received widespread recognition for its achievements and has become an important platform for showcasing the country's efforts to address climate change, the CCTV report said. During the same conference, Li also said that China will send a delegation to attend COP31 and will actively advance international climate negotiations. COP31 will conduct negotiations and consultations on nearly 100 agenda items related to the implementation of the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement, covering mitigation, adaptation, finance and just transition, per CCTV News. "As a responsible major developing country, China has consistently participated in and advanced international climate negotiations in a proactive and constructive manner," Li said, adding that China will contribute Chinese wisdom, solutions and strength to the success of COP31. Ma Jun, director of the Institute of Public and Environmental Affairs, told the Global Times that the gap between emission reduction pledges and real action remains wide, with current global efforts falling short of global climate targets and climate overshoot increasingly unavoidable. Geopolitical divisions fragment global governance, hinder climate cooperation and complicate efforts to balance energy, food and climate security, he noted. Some developing countries also struggle to balance climate mitigation and adaptation with economic growth and poverty alleviation, constrained by severe shortages of finance, technology and capacity, Ma added. The expert noted that China's sustained climate action offers a valuable lesson by integrating emissions reduction with pollution control and green transformation. Linking clean energy, energy-efficiency upgrades and electric vehicles with environmental improvement, resource recycling, industrial upgrading and job creation can address climate change while creating new sources of green growth. Through South-South cooperation, China can help other developing countries strengthen their capacity for independent climate action and reduce transition costs by sharing appropriate technologies, project experience and training. These lessons should, of course, be adapted to each country's resource endowments and stage of development, Ma noted. Li said during the press conference on Wednesday that China has built the world's largest and most complete clean energy industrial chain, with green and low-carbon industries becoming an important engine of economic growth, according to a report by the Xinhua News Agency. By the first half of 2026, the country's total installed renewable energy capacity reached 2.46 billion kilowatts, accounting for 60.7 percent of total national power generation capacity. At the end of July, installed solar power capacity surpassed coal power for the first time in history, making it China's largest single power source. Moreover, China's combined installed capacity of operational and approved nuclear power units has risen to first place in the world. New energy vehicle production and sales have ranked first globally for 11 consecutive years. On Wednesday, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment also released an annual report on China's policies and actions for addressing climate change 2026, outlining China's basic position and proposals for the COP31. "China will continue to play a proactive and constructive role, support Turkey in its capacity as the COP31 Presidency and Australia as the President of Negotiations, and work with other Parties in the spirit of a community with a shared future for humanity to ensure that COP31 focuses on implementation and cooperation," it reads.

artigo.texto: US solid-state battery maker QuantumScape, backed by Volkswagen and Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, is working with a South Korean equipment supplier. The development could expand the role of Korean companies beyond conventional lithium-ion batteries into the next-generation battery market. According to industry sources on Oct. 20, Mplus has developed assembly equipment for QuantumScape’s solid-state batteries and is conducting validation for mass production. QuantumScape completed its Eagle Line pilot production facility at its headquarters in San Jose, California, in February. The company is currently increasing sample production of its first commercial product, the QSE-5, at the facility. The uptime of key production equipment has exceeded 90%. Uptime refers to the proportion of available operating time during which equipment functions normally. “Among US solid-state and lithium-metal battery startups, QuantumScape has one of the most developed production infrastructures, including dry rooms,” an industry official said. “Because next-generation battery manufacturing processes differ among companies and mass-production viability has yet to be fully demonstrated, commercialization will depend on how quickly manufacturers can achieve sufficient production speeds and yields.” QuantumScape is supplying samples to Volkswagen’s battery subsidiary PowerCo and other companies to evaluate battery performance and practical applications. It has jointly developed next-generation batteries with Volkswagen since 2012 and has received more than $300 million in cumulative investment from the automaker. Volkswagen invested in QuantumScape to secure next-generation battery technology that could improve electric vehicle driving range and safety. Solid-state batteries replace the liquid electrolyte used in conventional lithium-ion batteries with a solid material. By eliminating flammable organic solvent-based liquid electrolytes, they reduce fire risks. They can also accommodate more energy within the same volume by reducing the components and space required to ensure internal battery safety. The core of QuantumScape’s technology is its proprietary ceramic separator. Conventional lithium-ion batteries use a porous separator between the cathode and anode, along with a liquid electrolyte that allows lithium ions to move between them. QuantumScape’s ceramic separator prevents direct contact between the electrodes while allowing lithium ions to pass through. The company has partnered with Corning and Murata to mass-produce the ceramic separators. Another distinguishing feature is its anode-free architecture. Instead of mixing and coating anode active materials such as graphite, the design uses only an anode current collector, reducing associated material and production costs. In QuantumScape’s manufacturing process, ceramic separators are laminated onto copper foil used as the anode current collector after the cathode electrode process. Cathodes are then attached to both sides to form individual units called monocells. The monocells are subsequently immersed in and removed from a solution containing catholyte, a liquid electrolyte that facilitates lithium-ion movement between cathode active materials. Multiple monocells are stacked to complete a battery cell. After packaging, QuantumScape simplifies the formation process, which stabilizes battery performance through initial charging and discharging, to reduce production time and costs. Beyond expanding its own manufacturing facilities, QuantumScape is pursuing a licensing business that would allow other companies to use its battery manufacturing technology. It has signed a technology licensing agreement with PowerCo covering battery production capacity of up to 85 GWh. QuantumScape is also considering outsourcing production line operations to external companies. It is reportedly holding related discussions with South Korean battery manufacturers. If its manufacturing technology expands to external production facilities, Mplus could secure additional equipment orders, having developed machinery tailored to QuantumScape’s processes. Mplus has secured equipment technologies required for QuantumScape’s battery manufacturing process. As with conventional lithium-ion batteries, the process involves notching, which cuts electrodes to specified dimensions; stacking, which layers multiple electrodes; and packaging, which encloses the cells in external materials. Mplus can supply a complete range of assembly equipment for these processes, as well as specialized high-temperature and high-pressure equipment required for solid-state battery production. Mplus has also diversified its customer base. SK On accounted for more than 80% of its revenue in 2022, but that share fell to approximately 22% in 2025, while other customers’ combined contribution rose to nearly half of revenue. The company has expanded its order base among US and European battery manufacturers. It recently supplied equipment for producing prismatic batteries for defense applications to a European battery company, believed to be France’s Saft. Mplus is pursuing additional orders and is reportedly close to signing a new contract. “We cannot confirm specific details concerning our customers,” an Mplus official said. “We intend to drive earnings growth by securing overseas customers and expanding new orders.” Mplus had an order backlog of 63.1 billion won at the end of the second quarter of 2026.

artigo.texto: When we asked writer-director Woody Bess what inspired Portal to Hell, his horror comedy about a gateway to hell that opens inside a laundromat, he pointed to grief. His college roommate died by suicide a couple of months into the pandemic, after the two had drifted apart, and Bess said he did not know his friend was struggling until he got the call. In the film, Trey Holland plays Dunn, a debt collector who finds the portal at his local laundromat. Richard Kind plays Chip, the demon who comes through it to drag Dunn’s neighbor, Mr. Bobshank, to hell over an unpaid debt, and Chip offers a deal: three souls in exchange for Bobshank’s. Keith David (The Thing) plays Bobshank, Romina D’Ugo plays laundromat attendant Ed, and Michael McDonald also stars. Bess wrote, directed and shot Portal to Hell, his feature debut. It premiered at Slamdance in 2025, won the Dangerous Visions Award at the Chattanooga Film Festival and played FrightFest, Calgary Underground and Vancouver Horror Show before Cineverse released it on Digital and VOD in the US on September 8, 2026. In a written interview, we asked Bess about his comedic influences, why the people in his film barely react to a portal to hell, and what the story means to him. His answers follow, lightly edited for spelling. Edgar Wright Was His Biggest Influence iHorror: The comedy of the movie is done really well. Did you have any major comedic inspirations when writing the script, be they movies, comedians, etc.? Woody Bess: I love Edgar Wright’s movies. I’d say that’s probably the single biggest inspiration. Shaun of the Dead is really funny, it’s got horror but it’s about a friendship at its core. Structurally, we ripped off Little Shop of Horrors. The Portal Stands In for Everyday Evils iHorror: A constant point of amusement for me was how casual everyone was about the things that were happening. A few times a character would note that there’s a portal to hell with the same level of import as one pointing at an uncommon, but not entirely rare butterfly. Did you write it this way only for comedic purposes, or were you trying to say something deeper? Woody Bess: For the Portal, people acknowledge it in the film but outside of Dunn and Ed, nobody really does anything about it. The idea behind it was to make a film about the mundane evils we encounter every day: our healthcare system, wealth inequality, wars, mass shootings, etc. Those are all evils we’ve learned to tolerate. They’re too big for any one person to fix and we all have bills to pay, we have our own problems. How people treat the portal in the film is the same numbness we’ve learned to get through the day. Dunn Believes People Are Black and White iHorror: I found Dunn’s moralizing interesting. You’ve said in other interviews that Dunn is not a dumb man (at least that’s not how Trey plays him), so why did you write him as trying to place everyone in a “good” or “bad” box? What can we learn from Dunn’s story in this regard? Woody Bess: We tried to keep it simple, mostly to keep costs down. There’s a book I love called Creating Character Arcs. In it, each character believes a lie that’s holding them back. For Dunn, it’s that people are black and white. The truth he has to embrace is that we’re all these messy gray blobs. We’re the heroes in our story and the villains in someone else’s. We’re hypocrites and liars and one bad day or bad decision away from being monsters. But also one good decision away from being angels. Ed Is a Friend Who Runs From Her Mistakes iHorror: If I view the movie as a metaphor, I feel like I understand the point of most of the elements. But one I haven’t quite understood is Ed. What was Ed meant to represent for Dunn? Or was she just meant to be a fun accomplice for Dunn on his demonic mission? Woody Bess: She wasn’t meant to represent anything but a friend for Dunn. I guess a part of the film is how we reconcile the mistakes we make. For Bobshank, it’s to give it all away and mind his own business. I think Ed represents the most common, which is to run from those mistakes. I feel like in 10 years or so she’d stop running and try to make amends head on. There will never be a sequel but if there was it’d probably be about that. A Friend’s Death Inspired the Film iHorror: I’m sure different viewers interpret this story differently. Some might see it as a fun, straightforward story about a hellish laundromat, while others might see it as a story about self-forgiveness, loneliness, and grief. Was this story personal for you and, if you’re comfortable talking about it, why? What inspired this? Woody Bess: My friend passed away by suicide a couple months into the pandemic. He was my college roommate and we used to do everything together. But I moved to LA after school and we grew apart. We talked less and less. When I got the call that he had died, I didn’t even know he was struggling. We can all fall into hells of our own making. Portal to Hell is available now on Digital and VOD in the US from Cineverse. If you or someone you know is struggling, you can call or text 988 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in the US. Fan verdict and scores by iHorror

artigo.texto: 'Chinese Battery Maker' CATL Shares Plunge 11% on Profitability Concerns Third-quarter revenue rose, but net profit grew just 14.5%, its lowest rate in two years China's consumption tax reinstatement and reduced export tax rebates weigh on results CATL, China's leading electric vehicle battery maker, saw its shares plunge as much as 11% intraday after reporting third-quarter results that fell short of market expectations. The increase in quarterly net profit slowed to 14.5%, its lowest level in about two years. According to Bloomberg on October 21, CATL shares fell as much as 11% in early trading on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and as much as 9.3% on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The declines followed the company's third-quarter results, announced on October 20, which fell short of market expectations. CATL's third-quarter revenue rose 58.6% year on year to 165.2 billion yuan (approximately 32.76 trillion won), while net profit increased 14.5% to 21.25 billion yuan (approximately 4.21 trillion won). The net profit growth rate was the lowest in about two years and well below the market forecast of 41.2%. Revenue surged, but profitability deteriorated because of rising costs and reduced tax benefits. China's tax reform plans are also weighing on the company. In July, the Chinese government ended a consumption tax exemption for lithium-ion batteries that had been in place for 10 years and began imposing a 2% consumption tax in September. It also reduced value-added tax rebates on battery exports and plans to eliminate them entirely starting in 2027. The measures are seen as an effort to curb overproduction and cutthroat competition in the battery industry. Markets expect the impact to extend beyond CATL, the industry leader, to small and midsize battery makers. Citigroup said, "If even CATL cannot fully pass the consumption tax burden on to its customers, it will be difficult for second-tier companies to absorb it." Inside the battery cell factory of Chinese battery maker CATL in Debrecen, Hungary, on October 1, 2026 (local time). AFP-Yonhap News View original image Automakers' efforts to reduce their dependence on CATL are also seen as a headwind. Some automakers are diversifying their suppliers by turning to small and midsize battery makers to reduce their reliance on CATL, intensifying price competition. CATL's shares on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange have fallen to about half their peak in May 2026. However, on its earnings conference call on October 20, CATL said it was "actively communicating" with customers to mitigate the impact together. The company added that it was "advancing new technologies and products to reduce the impact on profitability." CATL maintained a positive outlook for next year. The company said global demand for batteries used in electric vehicles and energy storage systems (ESS) "may not be as pessimistic as the market expects and has good growth potential." artigo.texto: - Third-quarter net profit rose 14.54% year-on-year, while revenue increased 58.58%. - Gross margin for the first 9 months was 22.72%, down from 25.31% a year earlier. CATL (HKEX: 3750), the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker, reported higher third-quarter net profit from a year earlier, but earnings fell from the second quarter as profit growth failed to keep pace with its business expansion. Net profit attributable to shareholders rose 14.54% year-on-year to 21.25 billion yuan ($3.16 billion) in the third quarter, according to financial results CATL released on Tuesday. That was down 5.77% from 22.55 billion yuan in the second quarter, CnEVPost calculations show. Third-quarter revenue rose 58.58% year-on-year to 165.22 billion yuan. Net profit attributable to shareholders excluding non-recurring gains and losses increased 14.86% to 18.86 billion yuan. For the first 9 months of the year, CATL's net profit attributable to shareholders rose 31.60% year-on-year to 64.53 billion yuan, while revenue increased 56.19% to 442.14 billion yuan. The company attributed its revenue growth over the period to business expansion. However, cost of sales rose faster than revenue, increasing 61.61% to 341.7 billion yuan. Gross margin for the first 9 months was 22.72%, down about 2.59 percentage points from 25.31% a year earlier, according to calculations based on revenue and cost of sales in the financial report. Research and development expenses rose 22.89% year-on-year to 18.52 billion yuan over the same period. Investment income increased 73.11% to 9.07 billion yuan, which the company said mainly reflected its share of investee companies' net profits. Despite the earnings growth, net cash generated from operating activities fell 23.60% year-on-year to 61.63 billion yuan in the first 9 months. As of the end of September, CATL's accounts receivable had risen 47.78% from the end of last year to 112.91 billion yuan, while inventories increased 53.15% to 144.77 billion yuan. The company attributed both increases to business expansion. CATL maintained its lead in the global EV battery market. Its global battery installations rose 25.2% year-on-year to 333.0 GWh in the first 8 months, according to South Korean market research firm SNE Research. Its global market share increased to 39.4% from 37.7% a year earlier, ahead of second-place BYD (HKEX: 1211) at 15.1%. China's battery market also continued to expand. Domestic power battery installations rose 14.7% year-on-year to 87.2 GWh in September, setting a new high for the year for the second consecutive month, according to the China Automotive Battery Innovation Alliance (CABIA). Energy storage batteries grew faster. China's energy storage battery sales rose 104.4% year-on-year to 73.5 GWh in September, accounting for 33.0% of combined power and energy storage battery sales. CATL ranked first in China's power battery market in September, with installations of 35.49 GWh and a market share of 40.92%. ($1 = 6.7200 yuan)

artigo.texto: SK Nexilis Develops Carbon-Coated Copper Foil for Next-Generation Batteries Improves Adhesion to Silicon Anode Materials to Prevent Electrode Delamination Also Suitable for Dry Electrode Processes Commercialization Targeted for the Second Half of 2027 SK Nexilis, the investment vehicle for SKC's copper foil business for secondary batteries, has developed copper foil for next-generation batteries that improves adhesion to silicon anode materials. The technology can extend battery life, improve safety, and be applied to dry electrode processes. Commercialization is targeted for the second half of 2027. SK Nexilis said on October 20 that it had successfully developed “high-adhesion carbon-coated copper foil,” a technology that coats the surface of copper foil with a special carbon material. The technology increases adhesion between copper foil and anode materials, helping suppress electrode delamination caused by the expansion of silicon anode materials. This is expected to improve the structural stability of electrodes and enhance battery life and safety. Recently, the battery industry has been increasing the silicon content of anode materials to boost energy density. However, silicon expands in volume during charging and discharging, making it important to ensure strong adhesion between copper foil and anode materials. The newly developed copper foil can also be used in dry electrode processes, which can reduce battery manufacturing costs and energy consumption. SK Nexilis said the material has strong potential for use in dry processes, where adhesion between electrode materials and copper foil is also important. SK Nexilis is currently validating process stability and plans to secure mass-production technology after establishing a pilot production system. artigo.texto: Samsung Asset Management's KODEX Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus Surpasses 200 Billion Won in Net Assets Samsung Asset Management's exchange-traded fund (ETF) focused on energy storage systems (ESS) and solid-state batteries has surpassed 200 billion won in net assets just four months after its listing, buoyed by inflows from individual investors. On October 21, Samsung Asset Management announced that its KODEX Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus ETF had surpassed 200 billion won in net assets. The milestone came four months after its listing on June 23, with net assets reaching 237.6 billion won as of the market close on October 20. The ETF's performance was driven by strong net buying from individual investors. Cumulative net purchases by individuals since its listing totaled 75.4 billion won, with approximately 23.3 billion won flowing in over the past month alone. Its return over the past month was 11.99%, and its return over the past three months was 34.98%, placing it among the top-performing ETFs listed in Korea. In particular, its return since listing was 6.88%, ranking first among battery and materials-related ETFs listed in Korea. This reflects the combination of expanding orders for Korean ESS companies and rising expectations for the commercialization of solid-state batteries. KODEX Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus invests in both solid-state batteries and ESS, the two growth pillars of the battery industry. Solid-state batteries use solid electrolytes instead of liquid ones, reducing fire risks and increasing energy density, making them a next-generation battery technology. ESS are systems that store electricity generated and supply it when needed. Applications for solid-state batteries and ESS are steadily expanding beyond the industry's traditional focus on electric vehicles to include humanoid robots, urban air mobility (UAM), and aerospace. The ETF allocates approximately 50% of its investments to LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI, leaders in the solid-state battery and ESS sectors. LG Energy Solution is targeting the North American market by successively bringing ESS production facilities in the United States online. Samsung SDI is preparing to mass-produce a new lithium iron phosphate (LFP)-based ESS product and solid-state batteries in the fourth quarter. The remaining half is invested across companies in the value chains of these two growth areas. The ETF includes ESS value-chain companies such as Sangsin EDP, Seojin System, HANJUNG NCS, and SFA Nexel, as well as solid-state battery value-chain companies such as Isu Specialty Chemical, Daejoo Electronic Materials, Lotte Energy Materials, POSCO Future M, and L&F. artigo.texto: ▲ Chinese EV battery manufacturer CATL The shares of CATL, the world's largest electric vehicle battery manufacturer, plummeted over 10 percent on the 21st local time following third-quarter earnings that fell short of expectations. Shares of other Chinese battery makers also showed a synchronized decline. According to Chinese portals such as Baidu, CATL's shares closed down 12.03 percent from the previous session at 227.9 yuan on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. This is about half of its peak of 460.0 yuan reached on May 6 on a closing price basis. On the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, where it is dually listed, CATL's shares also dropped 11.41 percent on the same day. CATL's market capitalization shrank from 1.22 trillion yuan (approximately 242.1 trillion won) the previous day to 1.07 trillion yuan (approximately 212.4 trillion won) as of the closing price. Amid intensifying competition in the EV battery market, CATL announced in its third-quarter earnings release the previous day that its net profit increased by 14.54 percent year-on-year to 21.25 billion yuan (approximately 4.2 trillion won). This figure fell significantly short of not only its second-quarter net profit growth rate but also the market consensus of 41.2 percent compiled by market research firm London Stock Exchange Group. It is also the lowest since the fourth quarter of 2024, when it recorded 13.6 percent. The South China Morning Post (SCMP) reported that CATL's shares have been on a downward trend since Chinese EV makers Xiaomi and Li Auto announced last month that they would cooperate with other battery manufacturers. In the market, there are also observations that automakers have recently shown a trend of moving away from CATL. Investment bank JPMorgan recently downgraded its investment rating on CATL's Hong Kong shares to "Neutral," citing that the profitability of China's EV industry is deteriorating faster than expected due to tax changes and other factors, which could affect demand for CATL battery products. Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, and others have warned of the possibility that market consensus forecasts could be lowered. According to Chinese media such as the Securities Times, CATL addressed concerns over demand that day by stating, "Demand is not that pessimistic," and adding that "industrial capacity utilization remains at a relatively high level." Regarding next year's battery demand, it stated that it is "still worth looking forward to." Regarding the 23.6 percent year-on-year decline in operating cash flow for the first three quarters, CATL stated that it was due to proactively adjusting payments to partner suppliers and does not affect the company's long-term cash generation capability. However, the market views that the resumption of China's battery consumption tax collection to prevent overcapacity and the reduction of value-added tax rebate rates for new energy vehicle exports will act as a burden on the earnings of CATL and the broader Chinese battery industry. Bloomberg reported that CATL's sluggish earnings are fueling concerns over Chinese battery companies. Citigroup analysts noted that CATL's latest earnings carry negative implications for other players as well, stating, "If CATL cannot do it, other companies will not be able to fully pass on the consumption tax." Other Chinese battery stocks also closed lower that day, including Gotion (-6.94%) and EVE (-5.27%) on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, and CALB (-3.57%) on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. artigo.texto: TORONTO, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HiTHIUM, an integrated full-scenario energy storage solutions provider, has announced its entry into the Canadian market. Ranked in the top two globally for energy storage component, the manufacturer has surpassed 200 GWh in cumulative delivered capacity, focusing exclusively on stationary energy storage technologies. Canada's energy storage expansion requires reliable large-scale suppliers and local presence Mizhi Zhang, HiTHIUM President of Global Business, commented: "We are committed to delivering Canadian customers advanced, robust solutions, from 8-hour long duration energy storage to extreme-weather-ready sodium-ion BESS. But this also means being present for customers wherever they are, able to serve them quickly and locally. While Toronto serves as the main hub for our Canadian operations, we have subsidiary offices in British Columbia and Alberta, as well as operating sites in Quebec, Yellowknife, and Fort Smith." HiTHIUM has introduced 4-hour and 8-hour BESS solutions to serve the market's rapid buildout of utility-scale energy storage. With installed Canadian storage expected to double between 2025 and 2027, and the country's total wind, solar, and energy storage capacity on track to reach 50 GW by 2035, HiTHIUM is positioned to fill the growing demand for BESS on a large scale. The company has also revealed a new 4 MWh sodium-ion storage solution, which is designed for an extra-long service life, supports storage durations from 2 to 8 hours, and is perfect for extremely cold climates, like Northern Canada. "Canada's ambitious clean energy targets, as well as its high safety and regulatory standards, require partners who can deliver advanced technology that's also tested and compliance-ready. At the same time, project developers have to consider the tough climate. As a vertically integrated, global solutions provider, HiTHIUM is structured to meet exactly this nexus of challenges. Our strategy of advancing both lithium-ion and sodium-ion storage is designed to offer customers in markets like Canada the benefits of flexibility, since we see these technologies as highly complementary," continued Zhang. "Our partners, whether major energy developers, public utilities, or industrial enterprises, rely on our readiness for local certification and our long-term bankability to support them, from permitting through project commissioning," added Jordan Hebbert, HiTHIUM Senior Manager of Canada. "Likewise, they depend on the proven durability of HiTHIUM technology-including performance even in extreme weather conditions. In fact, long-term operational data from North American and European projects has recently demonstrated systems outperforming even our guarantees. And we offer customers a wider range of durations and choice of chemistries because we understand that they're coming to us with a very diverse range of energy storage needs." 4-hour or 8-hour BESS: Matching duration to project specifications The manufacturer's 4-hour BESS solution consists of its "∞Power" 6.25 MWh container, built on HiTHIUM's own 1175 Ah cell. Most Canadian projects are currently designed around the 4-hour unit. This enables them to shift wind, solar, and baseload output to later peak times, strengthen grid reliability, and drive the consumption of more renewables, particularly as electrification increases demand. The ∞Power system design fits more capacity into the typical 20-foot container but also reduces a project's overall footprint, because the containers can be placed back-to-back and side-to-side. In a groundbreaking step for long duration energy storage, HiTHIUM also developed the first ever native 8-hour solution based on lithium-ion technology. Its 6.9 MWh 8-hour BESS, built with HiTHIUM's own 1300 Ah cells, fewer components overall, and a 25-year lifespan, is designed to address issues like curtailments and to fill key gaps for zero-downtime industrial segments like AI data centers. For wind project developers and data center operators alike, 8-hour BESS offers risk reduction and greater revenue reliability. Extreme fire test validates safety architecture HiTHIUM additionally worked with UL Solutions at the start of 2026 on an independently conducted, extreme fire test of its 6.25 MWh block's intrinsic safety systems. A container was subjected to 24 hours of extreme combustion conditions, with its doors opened for maximum thermal spread, while neighboring containers were placed just 15 cm away. Only the containers' passive safety systems were enabled. The results validated HiTHIUM's multi-layer safety architecture, with the tested container structurally intact after the test, no thermal propagation across the containers, and the temperatures of cells in adjacent containers remaining below safety thresholds.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich- CATL addressed recent investor concerns over demand for the new energy sector in 2027 in an investor relations filing dated October 20. From the company's vantage point, industry demand that year remains promising. CATL noted that while overall domestic passenger car sales dipped in 2026, the electrification rate is climbing rapidly. So is the average battery capacity per vehicle. As a result, the power battery market for domestic new energy passenger cars still managed positive growth. Image source: CATL Electrification among domestic commercial vehicles is accelerating as well. In Europe, the shift to electric power shows continuity, with a steady stream of competitive new models hitting the market. Meanwhile, the potential for electrification in other regions is gradually unlocking. Data shows domestic power battery installations climbed 17% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, while sales (including exports) surged 38%—growth driven largely by higher battery capacity per vehicle. The average battery capacity for new energy vehicles hit 69.5 kWh during that period, a 32% jump, with both pure electric and plug-in hybrid models seeing significant gains. Image source: Baidu Stock Tong CATL's response comes against a backdrop of sustained pressure on its stock price. As of October 21, shares had halved from their historical peak. Several brokerages have already trimmed their profit forecasts for CATL for 2027. Adding to the strain are shifts in tax policy: the value-added tax rebate on battery exports was cut from 9% to 6% starting April 1, 2026, and will be eliminated entirely on January 1, 2027. CATL indicated it is in talks with customers to share the burden of these policy shocks.

artigo.texto: By JENNIFER McDERMOTT A battery system installed in a Buffalo, New York, apartment building will store excess energy when it’s plentiful and power the building when the grid is strained and electricity is costly. The manufacturer and state officials hope it will show that larger batteries can safely operate where people live and work. The 3.75 megawatt-hour lithium-ion battery system, which can power the Peace Bridge Place affordable housing complex for several days, is among the largest battery systems in a U.S. residential building, manufacturer Viridi and developer Good Carbon Co. said Tuesday. “We want our electric power to be resilient, affordable and available. Distributed battery storage accomplishes all three,” Viridi CEO Jon M. Williams said. “The only thing that has been holding up installations at scale is safety; a lot of the products on the market over the last 10 years have burned things down.” Deploying large batteries that can safely power apartment buildings is an important step toward replacing fossil fuels with renewables, experts say, but they’re uncommon because of the cost and concerns about fire risks. Already, larger batteries are paired with solar and wind projects, and homeowners are using smaller batteries to store excess energy from rooftop solar and for backup power. How batteries help keep electricity flow steady Batteries help maintain a steady flow of power when sources such as solar and wind are not producing. They charge when the sun is shining or when wind is blowing. That energy can then be used when demand is high. Batteries can also store excess electricity from hydropower, and New York is one of the top hydropower-producing states. Buffalo is close to Niagara Falls, where most of the state’s hydropower is produced. When electricity demand is high, Peace Bridge will use the battery. It will get paid by the utility for not drawing from the grid and for sending power back if needed. This helps lower the complex’s overall electricity costs, which benefits residents. The building can use the system during outages, too. The New York State Energy Research and Development Agency helped fund the Peace Bridge Place project, as part of its focus on including disadvantaged communities in the clean energy transition. “It goes a long way toward demonstrating the safety and viability of these types of projects,” said NYSERDA President and CEO Doreen Harris. Viridi has manufacturing facilities in Buffalo and Richmond, California, where a state grant assisted with renovations. California Energy Commission Chair David Hochschild said he’s impressed with the company. More than two-thirds of California’s electricity comes from clean energy and batteries get a lot of credit for that, Hochschild said. As electricity demand grows, batteries help ensure the grid is reliable, reduce pollution and contain costs, he added. “I believe the battery industry is the single most important energy industry for the next several decades,” said Hochschild, who co-founded the Electric Innovation Initiative to use electricity instead of fossil fuels more broadly throughout the U.S. economy. Viridi’s system passed a ‘near impossible’ test As large battery fires have garnered attention, some communities have opposed further development. However, the failure rate for batteries has decreased as more are installed, according to the Electric Power Research Institute. Viridi spent six years and $10 million figuring out how to make a fireproof container for batteries. Half the cost was for batteries Viridi destroyed during testing. Viridi uses plates, pouches and spacing to isolate each battery cell. If one fails, the energy dissipates instead of spreading to the next battery, so that no gas, smoke, heat or fire escapes the container, Williams said. Jigar Shah, an expert in clean energy financing and deployment, said the Peace Bridge Place system is a milestone in overcoming safety concerns. To ensure nothing would catch fire when used inside a residence, Viridi’s system had to pass a test where the battery was forced to fail while a cheesecloth covered the container. The cheesecloth did not char or ignite, according to the test report record. Viridi announced in April it met stringent Underwriters Laboratories safety standards so its system could be installed indoors without adding additional fire suppression to a building. Shah, who led the Department of Energy’s Loan Programs Office during the Biden administration, said Viridi is the only company to consistently pass this “near impossible” test. Shah thinks far more U.S. homes will use batteries for backup power by 2030. The U.S. can meet much more electricity demand and avoid costly upgrades to the grid if batteries are strategically deployed, he added. New York and California officials want forward-thinking energy solutions Viridi and Good Carbon Co. chose the Peace Bridge apartments because the all-electric building uses a geothermal system for heating and cooling rather than natural gas and needed additional, resilient power. The electricity demand locally can exceed the available supply, so the utility National Grid supported the endeavor, Williams added. Peace Bridge is considered affordable housing because renters earn no more than 80% of the area’s median income, Good Carbon said. It said energy storage will be an important part of future multifamily housing projects. Viridi has been manufacturing in Buffalo since 2018. A medical research building in the city is using its battery system, too. Viridi’s plant could build enough battery packs in a year to supply energy for about 14,000 average U.S. homes for 24 hours, Williams said. Harris, at NYSERDA, said the state needs more options like this for maintaining a reliable grid and managing costs. Gov. Kathy Hochul has made that a priority. “If we don’t need to build generation, we can utilize the grid that we have more effectively, that’s extremely valuable to us,” she said. In California

artigo.texto: A TIM defendeu que o leilão da faixa de 6 GHz ocorra em "momento adequado e em linha com a evolução do 5G", discordando do planejamento da Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel) de realizar a licitação em 2028. O posicionamento foi manifestado pelo diretor de Assuntos Regulatórios da tele, Carlos Eduardo Franco, em audiência pública sobre a frequência de 6 GHz, realizada pela Anatel, em São Paulo, nesta quarta-feira, 21. Embora não tenha citado um ano específico para o leilão, o executivo ressaltou que o certame deve levar em conta a disponibilidade de equipamentos e os investimentos relacionados a outros editais de espectro em execução pelas operadoras. "O ecossistema de 6 GHz ainda está em fase inicial de implementação em escala", pontuou. "Até 2028, deve ser avaliada a evolução efetiva do ecossistema e dos ciclos tecnológicos em andamento. O calendário precisa ser compatível com a evolução tecnológica", acrescentou. Para a TIM, o edital também deve trazer previsibilidade econômica para as participantes do eventual leilão, levando em conta preço mínimo, garantias exigidas, compromissos e retorno esperado. "É recomendável que os parâmetros econômicos sejam conhecidos com antecedência. Maior transparência favorece o planejamento", ressaltou Franco. Data centers O executivo da TIM também sugeriu que o compromisso de investimento em data centers, proposto pela Anatel, seja substituído por obrigações de expansão de cobertura móvel e de redes de transporte em áreas desassistidas. Na semana passada, Claro e Vivo se posicionarem de forma parecida em audiência pública realizada em Brasília. Nesse ponto, Franco ainda disse que a obrigação de aporte em data centers nas regiões Norte, Nordeste e Centro-Oeste pode sobrepor investimentos privados e políticas públicas. Desse modo, indicou que o melhor caminho seria a priorização de obrigações mensuráveis de redes de telecomunicações. Ele também contestou a eventual criação de uma entidade para administrar os recursos que iriam para os data centers. "O objetivo de reduzir desigualdades regionais é relevante, mas o desenho merece uma avaliação cuidadosa quanto à complexidade e alocação dos recursos do certame", asseverou. Blocos de espectro Na audiência, levando em conta os 700 MHz da parte superior da frequência de 6 GHz, a TIM ainda propôs que o edital preveja três blocos nacionais de 200 MHz e um regional de 100 MHz. "Este desenho preserva os incumbentes e uma alternativa regional, reduz a fragmentação e promove o uso eficiente da faixa", apontou Franco. A consulta da Anatel, contudo sugere apenas dois lotes nacional de 200 MHz, um regional de 200 MHz (dividido em seis regiões) e outro regional de 100 MHz.

artigo.texto: Israel explores nuclear fusion as data centers drive demand for power A new Energy Ministry proposal would fund research into a technology that could eventually transform electricity generation. The recommended plan calls for up to NIS 1 billion over five to seven years, although commercial fusion remains a distant and uncertain prospect. Israel’s growing demand for electricity, driven in part by the expansion of data centers, is prompting the Ministry of Energy to explore a technology that could one day transform power generation. The ministry has proposed a long-term investment program in nuclear fusion, an emerging energy source that promises abundant electricity but remains far from commercial viability. The proposal outlines three possible levels of investment in domestic research and development. The most modest would allocate NIS 50 million to NIS 100 million over five years. A more ambitious program would invest NIS 500 million to NIS 1 billion over five to seven years, while the most expansive option would commit up to NIS 2 billion over a decade and include the construction of an experimental reactor. The ministry recommends the middle option. It would bring together public institutions, private companies and research organizations in joint consortia, with participation from Israeli defense contractors such as Rafael and Elbit. The plan also calls for a regulatory sandbox that would ease certain requirements during experimental work and greater involvement in international fusion research programs. The proposal is intended to help Israeli companies and research institutions develop expertise and become part of a global industry attracting growing investment. However, it remains a policy recommendation rather than an approved government program, and no funding has yet been allocated. The incoming government will ultimately decide whether to prioritize the field and how much public money to commit. Israel already has two startups working in the sector. nT-Tao is developing a compact fusion reactor, while FusionMantle is developing components for fusion systems. The ministry’s proposed program would seek to build on this base by bringing together companies, academic researchers and state-supported facilities. Israel’s defense industry could contribute technologies developed for other demanding applications. Rafael and Elbit, for example, have expertise in high-power lasers, including technologies relevant to laser-based interception systems such as Iron Beam. Such capabilities could prove useful in some areas of fusion research, alongside expertise in vacuum systems and other complex engineering challenges. Elbit and Israel Aerospace Industries also have experience in materials engineering and turning specialized materials into functional systems. The Soreq Nuclear Research Center, which houses a particle accelerator and other research infrastructure, could provide facilities to support development in the field. The government’s proposal reflects an effort to identify where Israel can contribute to a global industry before fusion power becomes commercially established. The country would not need to develop an entire reactor independently to participate. Specialized components, materials, research capabilities and engineering technologies could offer routes into the international supply chain. But the distance between laboratory research and a commercially viable power plant remains considerable. Fusion researchers must overcome difficult physical and engineering challenges before the technology can reliably deliver electricity at a competitive cost. The approximately 417 nuclear reactors operating worldwide generate electricity through nuclear fission, in which heavy atomic nuclei, such as uranium, split and release energy. Fission is an established technology, but it carries challenges involving radioactive waste and the risk of accidents that can release radioactive material. Nuclear fusion works in the opposite direction. Rather than splitting heavy nuclei, it combines light ones. In the most widely studied approach, nuclei of hydrogen isotopes, deuterium and tritium, fuse to form helium and release energy. Fusion powers the Sun and other stars, but reproducing the process in a controlled environment on Earth is exceptionally difficult. Hydrogen nuclei carry a positive electrical charge and repel one another. To bring them close enough to fuse, researchers must create extreme conditions, typically heating fuel to temperatures exceeding 100 million degrees Celsius. At these temperatures, the fuel becomes plasma, an electrically charged state of matter. Maintaining that plasma under the necessary conditions is a major challenge. Researchers must confine it long enough for fusion reactions to occur while managing the enormous heat and energy involved. Different approaches seek to achieve this through magnetic fields, lasers or other methods. The energy balance is another critical hurdle. Fusion reactions can release substantial energy, but a practical power plant must generate more usable energy than the entire system consumes, while operating reliably and economically. In 2022, researchers at the U.S. National Ignition Facility achieved a landmark result when the energy released by fusion reactions exceeded the laser energy delivered to the target. The experiment demonstrated an important scientific breakthrough, but it did not mean that a fusion power plant had achieved net electricity production. The energy required to run the facility and the broader system remained much greater than the energy delivered by the lasers to the target. That distinction helps explain why fusion, despite decades of research, has yet to become a commercial source of electricity. The prospect of a new source of abundant, low-carbon electricity has attracted growing investment, particularly as data centers and AI infrastructure increase demand for power.
