artigo.texto: FAYETTEVILLE, N.C. (WTVD) -- The future of a proposed data center in Fayetteville remains uncertain after a special City Council session Monday morning drew a crowd of concerned residents demanding transparency and answers. Dozens filled the council chamber, some holding signs reading "Moratorium now, do the right thing," as city leaders debated next steps for a project that has been the subject of heated discussion in the community for the past eight months. After nearly two hours, the council scheduled another public hearing to further discuss the draft moratorium and agreed to consult an attorney to revise the proposed ordinance language, leaving many attendees frustrated by the lack of clear resolution. "They're flying the plane while they're building it," said Christi Davis, an Eastover resident who lives just 1.1 miles from a proposed data center site. "The deal, it's got to go through a bunch of hoops to get passed. But Fayetteville, if the landowner requests annexation, then Fayetteville's rules apply. Right now, Cumberland County's rules apply, and it's agricultural land at the moment." The council's deliberations come after a 120-day study, launched in April, which included tours of data centers in North Carolina and Virginia and consultations with industry experts. According to city officials, three community sessions have been held, with water use, noise, and power emerging as residents' top concerns. Councilmember Shaun McMillan voiced frustration about the lack of preparedness and transparency: "I would love to understand why we didn't have the advanced materials both in text and in PowerPoint form prior to this meeting," he said. Despite a lengthy presentation, many residents left the meeting feeling their questions had gone unanswered. Nubian "King" Holmes, a Fayetteville resident, said, "They were unprepared, nor did they have answers to simple yes or no questions. How do you vote on something like that? There are too many things at stake. There are too many people's livelihood and health at risk." Davis echoed the sentiment, expressing dissatisfaction with the council's approach. "They should have gone on and voted the moratorium because all this stuff is taking time and they're seeing it. And this they can't even agree," she said. "They're jumping the gun. They're flying the plane while they're building it. And that's why we need the moratorium to give us time to set this stuff in motion." The City Council plans to draft a moratorium ahead of its next work session, scheduled for November. The conversation is far from over as residents and officials continue to debate the project's effects and the city's path forward.

artigo.texto: It was deju vu all over again on Tuesday night when the Little Rock City Board of Directors failed on a 4-4 vote to pass a six-month moratorium on data center projects. The board took up this issue in August, when some members tried to pass an 18-month moratorium. But the board made the same vote, with the same directors voting the same way. Six votes are needed to pass an ordinance. The ordinance being considered Tuesday would have given the city time to set up restrictions and regulations relating to water, noise, emergency infrastructure, zoning regulations and monitoring relating to data center projects. The urgency to pass an ordinance comes at a time when Google is planning to build a $1 billion data center at the Port of Little Rock. Both measures were sponsored by Director Kathy Webb, and at both meetings, Jay Chesshir, head of the Little Rock Regional Chamber, came in like a relief pitcher to finish the deal, appearing to scare away anyone considering voting with the “yes” contingent with threats that a moratorium could mean legal trouble for the city. One of the “no” votes came from Webb’s friend, Director Capi Peck, who was listed in the agenda handout as a co-sponsor of the moratorium ordinance. After Peck voted against Webb’s 18-month moratorium back in August, she took heat on social media for her action. Webb seemed to be expecting a different outcome this week. In a text exchange earlier in the day, she was asked if she thought the measure would pass. “I think so!” she wrote back. “Four sponsors including me.” After the meeting, Webb said the vote caught her by surprise. “It was a shock,” she said. “It was not expected.” She said she thought she had five votes going into the meeting and was hoping to peel off one of the at-large directors. Asked if she was done with trying to get a moratorium passed, she said possibly, but that she had made a promise when the board passed an ordinance regulating data centers in June to make improvements to that measure. “I keep my promises,” she said. A half-dozen citizens spoke in support of the passage of the ordinance, with one person speaking against it. Then came time for the directors to speak. Peck confirmed she was a co-sponsor – giving Webb credit for the lion’s share of the work – and said she had read over the measure and marked it up several times. In the end, though, she said she still found it to be “pretty technical.” She then invited Brad Jordan, director of Planning and Development for the city, to the microphone, asking him if his department could handle everything that would be required to implement the ordinance. “Whatever we’re asked to do, we’ll do it and we’ll do it well,” he said. He went on to say that getting it done in such a short period of time would be challenging. “It means for the next year, we’ll be doing this,” he said. Director Dean Kumpurus, instead of immediately giving his thoughts, invited Chesshir to speak, a move that brought a few grumbles from the crowded chamber. Chesshir also spoke against the 18-month moratorium. Chesshir’s main argument was that most of what was covered in Webb’s legislation would already be dealt with by one of several local, state or federal agencies, such as the state health department and the Arkansas Division of Environmental Quality, as well as the federal Environmental Protection Agency. To pass an ordinance that conflicts with those agencies would be to invite “legal and litigation risk,” Chesshir said. In all, Directors B.J. Wyrick, Virgil Miller Jr. and Andrea Lewis joined Webb in voting for the measure, while Directors Lance Hines, Kumpuris and Joan Adcock joined Peck in voting against it. Director Antwan Phillips abstained.

artigo.texto: Uriel Renovables completes two 10 MW battery storage plants in the United States Uriel Renovables and Silo Energy have finished building two battery storage plants in Framingham and Chicopee, Massachusetts. The installations, backed by a $20 million investment, fall under the Clean Peak Standard program. Uriel Renovables has completed construction of two battery energy storage system (BESS) plants in Framingham and Chicopee, in the state of Massachusetts. The company operates through its U.S. subsidiary Uriel Renewables, alongside its local partner Silo Energy. Battery storage is also advancing elsewhere in the United States, including the two battery storage contracts won by Flatiron Energy in the Bronx and the 3.75 MWh system installed by Viridi and Good Carbon in Buffalo. Both units are in the commissioning phase, according to Uriel Renovables. 10 MW of power and 40 MWh of capacity Each plant has a power rating of 5 MW with a duration of 4 hours, equal to 20 MWh of capacity per installation. Together, they represent 10 MW of power and 40 MWh of capacity. The two units required an investment of $20 million, the company said. The plants will store energy during hours of lowest demand and release it to the grid during periods of high consumption. Uriel Renovables says they will contribute to the stability of the New England power system. They would also make it easier to integrate a larger share of renewable energy into the grid. The projects fall under the Clean Peak Standard Both projects fall under the Clean Peak Standard, a program through which Massachusetts encourages clean energy to cover the hours of highest demand. The installations will earn certificates for the energy they feed into the grid during those consumption periods. Electricity suppliers will purchase a growing percentage of these certificates. The inauguration ceremony for the Framingham plant, located in Middlesex County, took place on September 30. State representatives, members of the Framingham municipality, and executives from the financing banks, engineering firms, contractors and other companies involved in the project attended. Ignacio Huarte, president of Uriel Renovables, and Juan FÃ©lix Huarte, president of Uriel Inversiones, the group's parent company, were present along with members of the management team. Ignacio Huarte said the two plants were the company's "first step" in the U.S. storage market and "a firm commitment" to Massachusetts. He added that storage allows renewables to meet demand when it is highest. Jorge Romero, country manager of Uriel Renovables, thanked the Framingham authorities and the company's partners, who made both projects possible. - Gas44.1 % - Nuclear16.1 % - Coal15.7 % - Solar10.6 % - Wind8.3 % - Hydro3.5 % - Bioenergy0.9 % - Other fossil0.5 % - Other renewables0.4 %

artigo.texto: Ørstedhave announced their innovative large-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) has officially completed construction. The system is designed to support the Hornsea 3 Offshore Wind Farm, located off the Norfolk coast. As part of the construction programme, 170 Megapacks have been installed alongside the project’s onshore converter station. Once fully operational, the facility, known as Iceni, will have a capacity of 600 MWh, enough to power an estimated 80,000 UK homes. Beatrice d’Eufemia, Project Manager for the Iceni BESS at Ørsted, said: “The system will make the best use of renewable energy produced in the UK. When electricity generation exceeds demand, the excess can be stored and then used when demand is greater.” According to Ørsted, the BESS is located separately from the Hornsea 3 onshore converter station and is connected by 18 x 33 kV cables, each approximately 600 metres long. Richard Swann, Construction Manager for the Iceni BESS at Ørsted, said: “It’s a real testament to the hard work, dedication and co-operation of teams from many different organisations that construction has been completed successfully.” The project will now move into the final stages of mechanical and electrical installation ahead of commissioning. artigo.texto: Huawei automotive unit joins CATL network with 2,520 stations — Electrek In China, Huawei’s automotive unit Yinwang, also known as Newcool, has entered into a framework agreement on strategic cooperation with battery manufacturer CATL and its subsidiary CAES. The agreement provides for the use of swappable batteries and vehicle compatibility with CATL’s Choco-swap network, which has 2,520 stations in around 200 Chinese cities. As Electrek reports, CATL plans to adapt vehicles with Huawei’s Qiankun intelligent driving systems for Choco-swap stations. The company wants to connect the vehicle, station and cloud services so that the system determines a car’s energy needs based on battery condition and driver habits, finds a station and independently directs the vehicle for a battery swap. Battery swap in 99 seconds According to CATL, the battery swap itself at a station can take 99 seconds. CATL Chairman Robin Zeng and Huawei Senior Vice President and Yinwang CEO Jin Yuzhi took part in signing the agreement. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram. Huawei owns 80% of Yinwang, while Seres and Changan-affiliated Avatr hold 10% each. Seres produces premium SUVs under the AITO brand, while Qiankun systems are also used by other Chinese automakers. Expansion of the Choco-swap network CATL entered the battery-swapping market in 2022 with the EVOGO service and relaunched this business under the Choco-swap brand with standardized battery packs at the end of 2024. At the end of 2025, the network had 1,020 stations; in early July, the number exceeded 2,000, and as of September 29, it reached 2,520. CATL is building more than 200 battery-swap stations per month and aims to increase their number to more than 3,000 by the end of the year. Other network partners include GAC, BAIC and NIO. At the same time, the agreement with Yinwang is a framework agreement: specific vehicle models, launch timelines and service regions have not been announced.

artigo.texto: Dan Cox demands statewide ban on new Maryland mega data centers ADAMSTOWN, Md. (WBFF) — Community members and Republican gubernatorial candidate Dan Cox met Wednesday to address the expansion of mega data centers and concerns that power transmission lines could take farmland and other private property through eminent domain. WBFF has been following mounting concerns from Adamstown residents about how these large-scale developments affect families, farmers, and property owners. Local voices highlighted the loss of farmland, air and water quality issues, noise, traffic, and worries about children’s health, particularly with hundreds of diesel generators near Carroll Manor Elementary School, where 500 students attend classes close to ongoing construction. ALSO READ | Gov. Candidate Dan Cox Criticizes Key Bridge Rebuild Delays "With the taking of our farmland, the taking of our property, the taking of our air quality, the taking and the sucking of our water supplies and the endangering of our children," Cox said at the press conference. He attributed fast-tracked permits for these facilities to decisions by Gov. Wes Moore and Frederick County Executive Jessica Fitzwater and called for immediate statewide action, including halting current and future mega data center approvals. He described the fast-track process as “many times done with NDAs or non-disclosure agreements,” and argued this was “unconscionable and it's harmful to the community.” Cox pointed to reports of air pollution, dust, water contamination and increased traffic, saying state and county officials had ignored the community’s pleas for help. The candidate proposed a statewide ban, a temporary moratorium on new data center development and a mandatory review of existing permits and environmental impacts. He said a governor could issue an executive order to enact a moratorium while pursuing legislation for a permanent ban. He argued current policies do not adequately protect communities, saying, “We need a statewide ban on new mega data centers. We need to enforce the law in Adamstown and across Maryland, and we need to have remedies for established harm and protect the families and children who live here.” Watch his Oct. 21 press conference in the video above. Local resident Hope Green, whose property borders a data center, described persistent dust, air pollution, and chemicals in her water: "As the county has identified, by the way, forever chemicals have been found in at least six wells in this area.” Green said the conditions have damaged her home's value, making it hard to sell, and she has received no compensation or buyout offer. Gene Butler, a third-generation landowner and farmer, described work noise and spotlights from the facility shining into his home at night. “We've had accidents, we've had people trespassing, the lights. It's just mind-blowing what they're getting away with," Butler said. He also shared concerns about possible effects on livestock and his inability to move his family business because of costs and declining property values. ALSO READ | Moore, Cox clash on bridge rebuild, crime and taxes in first Maryland governor debate Elyse Wilson, an Adamstown resident and advocate, noted the large impact of the diesel generators, saying that, on average, they are "about the size of a 26-foot moving truck." Wilson called for air quality monitoring around homes, not just the school, and said, “We just want not just Adamstown to be safe, but Maryland to be safe and the environment to be safe.” She cited other states, like Virginia, which have implemented stricter monitoring requirements and noted that local requests for similar measures have gone unanswered. "It's here. It's not going away. But we're trying to tell the rest of Frederick County and the state of Maryland what could happen to them. We don't want to see it," Green told FOX45's Maxine Rose following the press conference. Additional speakers said eminent domain for new transmission lines would take private property and farmland, affecting families across Frederick County and beyond. “It's not just going to be an Adamstown issue; it's going to be a Brunswick issue. It's going to be a Jefferson issue," said Frank Hollewa, a candidate for Frederick County council. "You got power lines that are going through district two, where it's going to destroy land through eminent domain. And people are just saying, 'Help me.'” Several called for meaningful compensation, independent assessments, and fair buyouts for affected property owners. Others warned about water and air pollution, potential health risks from diesel exhaust and damage to the region’s rural character. Cox criticized state and local leaders for what he called a lack of transparency and poor communication about these kinds of projects, citing reports of non-disclosure agreements and a community benefits agreement that local residents and candidates described as insufficient. He pledged to review permits issued for such developments and said he would seek to rescind state water and environmental permits. He also proposed independent, repeated testing of affected wells; monitoring for dust, noise and light; and practical assistance for families when testing and health guidance establish a need. Well, certainly under this condition I don't support that.” He said today’s mega data centers are on a different scale and have a different impact than when the legislation passed. Residents called on elected officials to listen, prioritize safety, and “do the right thing to help us.”

artigo.texto: Avaliação de Data Center de IA do Condado de Grant Expõe uma Lacuna de Relatórios de Nove Dígitos O Condado de Grant descobriu mudanças não reportadas em propriedades de data centers de IA, incluindo uma ampliação estimada em mais de US$ 100 milhões. A avaliação de data center de IA do Condado de Grant agora levanta uma questão básica: os registros tributários locais conseguem acompanhar campi computacionais cada vez mais complexos? A descoberta não estabelece automaticamente fraude tributária, ocultação deliberada ou um valor final de impostos não pagos. As informações publicamente disponíveis ainda não resolveram esses pontos. Elas mostram, porém, que mudanças físicas importantes estavam ausentes das informações usadas pelos avaliadores locais. Essa distinção importa em Quincy, Washington, onde Microsoft e diversos operadores de colocation construíram grandes campi em torno de energia hidrelétrica barata e acesso à fibra óptica. Os data centers se tornaram centrais para a base tributária local, tornando registros imobiliários precisos mais do que uma questão administrativa. O Condado de Grant agora precisa determinar quando cada melhoria passou a ser tributável, como ela deve ser avaliada e se avaliações anteriores exigem correção. Os operadores podem contestar essas decisões, como vários proprietários de data centers de Quincy já fizeram antes. Portanto, o conflito é maior do que uma estrutura negligenciada. A infraestrutura de IA está se expandindo mais rapidamente, tornando-se mais densa e incorporando equipamentos mais especializados. Os sistemas locais de avaliação ainda dependem de licenças, declarações dos proprietários, inspeções físicas e comunicação precisa entre departamentos. O Que Encontrou a Avaliação de Data Center de IA do Condado de Grant A principal constatação é uma lacuna de relatórios, e não ainda uma decisão tributária final. Segundo a investigação local inicial, autoridades do condado identificaram mudanças em data centers que não haviam sido reportadas para avaliação. Uma única ampliação foi estimada em mais de US$ 100 milhões. Esse valor parece descrever o valor de uma melhoria, e não uma cobrança tributária confirmada. Valor avaliado e imposto sobre propriedade são medidas diferentes. Os distritos tributários aplicam alíquotas aos valores avaliados depois de considerar isenções, classificações e outras regras. O registro público também não estabelece por quanto tempo a ampliação permaneceu fora do cadastro de avaliação. Esse cronograma influenciará se o condado pode ajustar avaliações anteriores e quanto de receita adicional poderá resultar disso. Os avaliadores de Washington avaliam imóveis, incluindo edifícios qualificados e melhorias permanentes. As empresas também declaram bens pessoais tributáveis mantidos em 1º de janeiro. Em um data center, essa distinção pode separar um edifício de servidores, sistemas elétricos e outros ativos móveis. O calendário publicado pelo Condado de Grant informa que os proprietários devem apresentar seus relatórios de bens pessoais ao avaliador. Enquanto isso, licenças de construção e inspeções físicas ajudam o condado a identificar mudanças em imóveis. Um campus hyperscale complica ambos os processos. Sua estrutura visível representa apenas uma parte do investimento. Distribuição de energia, sistemas de resfriamento, geradores, subestações, equipamentos de rede e instalações de servidores podem chegar por meio de projetos separados. A propriedade também pode ser dividida entre um proprietário de terreno, operador da instalação, empresa de nuvem e inquilino. Uma licença pode identificar uma parte, enquanto o equipamento tributável pertence a outra. Isso cria vários possíveis pontos de falha. Uma estrutura concluída pode não chegar prontamente ao avaliador. Uma declaração do proprietário pode omitir uma instalação. Os registros também podem classificar uma melhoria de forma diferente do tratamento final dado pelo avaliador. As evidências atuais não identificam qual explicação se aplica a cada discrepância no Condado de Grant. Seria prematuro descrever o caso como evasão intencional sem registros que o sustentem ou uma constatação oficial. No entanto, a escala elimina qualquer possibilidade de que se tratasse de uma questão trivial de documentação. Uma melhoria avaliada em mais de US$ 100 milhões pode alterar materialmente a avaliação de uma parcela e a distribuição das obrigações tributárias locais. A próxima etapa é a conciliação. A equipe do condado precisará comparar licenças, registros de inspeção, declarações de propriedade, datas de conclusão e fichas de avaliação anteriores. Os operadores devem ter a oportunidade de fornecer documentação e contestar qualquer valor proposto. Esse processo pode produzir uma avaliação mais alta sem gerar um aumento idêntico na receita do governo local. O sistema de alíquotas de Washington inclui limites de taxa e cálculos específicos por distrito que podem redistribuir as cargas tributárias entre proprietários. Ainda assim, incluir o valor omitido no cadastro é importante. Isso garante que grandes propriedades industriais recebam o mesmo escrutínio esperado de residências, fazendas, lojas e outras empresas. Por Que Uma Ampliação de Nove Dígitos Pode Ficar Fora do Cadastro Tributário Os data centers de IA expõem os limites de sistemas de avaliação projetados para ciclos de construção mais lentos e visíveis. Um projeto industrial convencional geralmente segue uma sequência reconhecível. O proprietário apresenta planos, obtém licenças, conclui inspeções e inaugura um edifício finalizado. Essa sequência cria várias oportunidades para que o avaliador identifique novo valor tributável. Os campi modernos de data centers nem sempre se desenvolvem de maneira tão organizada. Os operadores adicionam salas, sistemas de resfriamento, pátios elétricos, geradores e capacidade de servidores em fases sobrepostas. artigo.texto: Abrint e Abranet questionam obrigação ligada a data centers no leilão de 6 GHz Entidades cobram avaliação da sustentabilidade das instalações, dos efeitos concorrenciais e das obrigações previstas no edital. Abrint e Abranet questionaram a sustentabilidade econômica e os efeitos concorrenciais das obrigações de infraestrutura digital previstas na proposta de leilão de 6 GHz. Em audiência pública da Anatel hoje, 21, em São Paulo, as entidades pediram revisão dos critérios para implantação de data centers edge, esclarecimentos sobre sua operação e avaliação dos impactos sobre as empresas do setor. Pela Abrint, Cristiane Sanches defendeu que o desenho considere o retorno financeiro e a continuidade das instalações. Já o representante da Abranet, Eduardo Parajo, cobrou aprofundamento dos estudos jurídicos, econômicos e concorrenciais que fundamentam a vinculação desses investimentos à licitação de espectro. “Não basta construir essas instalações. É necessário demonstrar que haverá demanda, que a localização disponível é tecnicamente adequada, que os custos operacionais serão sustentáveis, e que existirá um modelo de exploração capaz de manter esses ativos funcionando ao longo do tempo”, afirmou Parajo. A pedido do setor, a consulta pública foi prorrogada pelo Conselho Diretor da Anatel até 7 de dezembro. Em novembro, acontecerá outra audiência pública presencial, em Fortaleza. Localização e continuidade Cristiane questionou a relação entre os critérios de localização dos data centers e as condições necessárias para manter sua operação. Segundo a representante da Abrint, a ausência desse tipo de infraestrutura em uma localidade não significa, necessariamente, que os operadores da região enfrentem um problema de conectividade. “A partir do momento em que eu tenho localidades desprovidas desse tipo de infraestrutura, e eu tenho a necessidade de continuidade futura daquela operação, eu posso ter um problema no edital de alocação desses próprios recursos”, afirmou. A representante da Abrint também questionou a aplicação do conceito de adicionalidade ao modelo proposto. Na avaliação apresentada, os critérios precisam ser examinados em conjunto com a viabilidade econômica das instalações e os compromissos financeiros dos vencedores. A Abranet, por sua vez, pediu que o edital esclareça as responsabilidades ao longo da operação. “É fundamental esclarecer quem será o responsável pela propriedade, operação, manutenção e atualização dos centros de dados”, afirmou Parajo. A entidade questionou ainda quem assumirá o risco de demanda insuficiente. Fundamento jurídico e concorrência A Abranet argumentou que redes móveis e centros de processamento de dados envolvem atividades e mercados distintos. Por isso, solicitou demonstração da necessidade, da proporcionalidade e dos benefícios públicos da obrigação. “Nós entendemos que é indispensável esclarecer o fundamento jurídico da conversão do valor econômico da outorga em investimentos dessa natureza”, disse Parajo. A associação também pediu avaliação dos efeitos sobre empresas independentes de hospedagem, colocation, processamento e interconexão. Segundo a manifestação, diferenças de custos, financiamento e obrigações regulatórias podem afetar as condições de competição entre os agentes.

artigo.texto: CATL has unveiled a dual-battery system for heavy-duty electric trucks, combining a swappable main pack with a separate backup battery to help operators use more energy between stops. Presented in Beijing on October 20, the technology arrives alongside an expansion of CATL’s Qiji battery-swapping network and new Tectrans II truck batteries. The setup pairs a chassis-mounted main battery, available in 432 kWh or 513 kWh configurations, with a fixed 77 kWh battery behind the cab. Both power sources are batteries, so the range-extender function remains fully electric. CATL says conventional swapping trucks often return with around 30 percent charge remaining. Its backup pack allows drivers to use more than 95 percent of the main battery’s capacity, with power switching between packs within milliseconds. The intended benefit is greater use of the battery capacity fleets already lease, while retaining an energy reserve for reaching a swap station. CATL says its upgraded Qiji station completes swaps in five minutes. The company targets 900 truck swapping stations by the end of 2026 and 2,000 in 2027, with a longer-term ambition of 10,000 across China. A revised battery rental billing method also lets operators retain the benefit of regenerative braking. CATL claims this can reduce per-kWh rental costs by up to 20 percent for customers on basic plans. Alongside the dual-battery launch, CATL introduced Tectrans II variants for different freight applications. These include lighter packs for short-haul operations, thinner batteries for construction trucks and a configuration suited to shorter-wheelbase vehicles. A separate long-range version offers 760 kWh capacity, an 800-volt architecture and a claimed driving range exceeding 600 kilometers. Agreements announced at the event covered an initial 13,000 units, underlining commercial interest in CATL’s expanding truck battery and swapping ecosystem. [source: CarNewsChina]

artigo.texto: Battery banks are (rightfully) getting a bit of a reputation on planes these days, so safer, more stable options are needed. Enter the LASER ChargeCore Powerbank range using new semi-solid state battery tech, offering enhanced battery safety and stability. LASER has been at the forefront of powerbanks, even introducing the newer LiFePO4 batteries to their battery banks last year, and are now introducing semi-solid state batteries with a focus on safety and peace of mind. Chris Lau, Managing Director of LASER said “We’ve been closely following semi solid state battery development for some time, since first visiting an EV factory several years ago, and advancements since that time mean that it can now move into smaller, more compact options. Simply put, I believe that Semi Solid State chemistry makes this the safest powerbank technology available in Australia today. We are focused on safety and peace of mind, and we know that it is a huge concern for Australian consumers these days when buying powerbanks.” The new ChargeCore PowerBanks come in three capacities, 10,000mAh, 20,000mAh and 27,000mAh offering a USB Type-C and two USB-A ports giving you versatile charging for your phones, tablets and more. The 10k and 20kmAh PowerBanks are able to deliver 20W of power across the three ports, while the 27,000mAh option can charge devices at up to 35W. All three models include an easy-to-read digital battery display showing how much is left, as well as including integrated protection against overcharging, overcurrent, short circuits and overheating. The new ChargeCore PowerBanks are available now in Black, with LASER also announcing Galactica, Grey, and Dark Cherry colour options are coming soon for their 10K and 20K ChargeCore PowerBanks. While the ChargeCore range is arriving now, LASER is also looking ahead, with Magnetic Charging and Waterproof options also using the semi-solid state battery tech coming soon. You can find the new ChargeCore Everyday Semi Solid State Series at Harvey Norman and Laser Online. The 10,000mAh with 20W USB-C PDis priced at .95, while the 20,000mAh with 20W USB-C PD is priced at .95. Lastly, the 27,000mAh ChargeCore PowerBank with 35W USB-C PD charging is priced at .95. artigo.texto: President Donald Trump said that data center companies should pay local communities a "dividend" to make their projects "popular." In a Truth Social post early Wednesday, Trump urged companies to "MAKE DEALS," but did not provide details on how much money they should return to communities or individuals where data centers are being built. "I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck," he wrote in the post. There's been a growing backlash against data center construction across the US, with some saying the projects are noisy, raise electricity bills, and compromise the general quality of living. Data centers are becoming an increasingly important issue in next month's midterm elections, and some politicians have shifted how they talk about the projects in recent months. Data Center Watch, a research project run by 10a Labs, found that in the first quarter of this year, at least 75 data center projects were delayed or canceled due to local opposition. Some companies have already started trying to placate unhappy locals with money or discounts. This summer, Elon Musk's SpaceX offered eligible Memphis residents a 50% discount on its Starlink internet service, tied to its growing AI build-out in the city. NorthPoint Development opted for a pure cash incentive and said it would pay every household in a Pennsylvania township $10,000 if it got permission to build a data center, the Wall Street Journal reported last month. In his Wednesday post, Trump also referenced one of his previous efforts: having tech companies cover their power costs when they build data centers to help keep local electricity prices flat. Several tech leaders agreed to do so in March, when they signed the "Ratepayer Protection Pledge," which mandates that companies provide or pay for the power generation and electricity needed for their AI projects, among other commitments. Trump closed his Wednesday post by saying that building data centers under his newest stipulations would be "GREAT FOR THE U.S.A."

artigo.texto: Data centers podem abrir novo mercado para vanádio brasileiro, diz Largo Em entrevista ao Mapa da Mina, co-CEO da mineradora destaca crescimento da demanda por baterias de fluxo e avanço do fornecimento de vanádio aos Estados Unidos A expansão dos data centers, impulsionada pelo avanço da inteligência artificial, pode abrir um novo mercado para o vanádio produzido no Brasil. A avaliação é do co-CEO da mineradora canadense Largo, Alberto Arias, que afirmou, em entrevista ao Mapa da Mina, programa de mineração da CNN, que a demanda pelo mineral para fabricação de baterias de armazenamento de energia tem crescido nos Estados Unidos. A companhia opera a mina Maracás Menchen, na Bahia, considerada uma das principais operações de vanádio do mundo. O mineral é utilizado principalmente na fabricação de aços de alta resistência e ligas metálicas para as indústrias de defesa e aeroespacial, mas vem ganhando espaço em tecnologias de armazenamento de eletricidade. “Fizemos muitos investimentos em baterias nos EUA. Criamos uma joint venture com uma produtora de baterias e, nos últimos dois anos, essa empresa está vendo um aumento exponencial de demanda de baterias de vanádio na indústria de data centers”, afirmou Arias. O executivo se refere à Storion Energy, empresa criada em 2025 a partir de uma parceria entre a Largo e a americana Stryten Energy. A companhia desenvolve componentes e eletrólitos utilizados em baterias de fluxo de vanádio, tecnologia voltada ao armazenamento de energia por períodos prolongados. Diferentemente das baterias convencionais de íons de lítio, as baterias de fluxo armazenam energia em soluções líquidas que contêm vanádio e circulam entre tanques e células eletroquímicas. A tecnologia permite armazenar grandes quantidades de eletricidade por várias horas, com longa vida útil e menor risco de incêndio. Por isso, é considerada uma alternativa para instalações industriais, redes elétricas e data centers, que precisam de fornecimento contínuo de energia para manter servidores e sistemas de processamento funcionando. O crescimento dessas instalações, especialmente das estruturas dedicadas à inteligência artificial, exige investimentos cada vez maiores em geração, transmissão e armazenamento de eletricidade. Para a Largo, esse movimento pode ampliar o consumo de vanádio, tradicionalmente concentrado na indústria siderúrgica. Arias afirmou que convidou representantes da parceira americana para conhecer a operação da Largo na Bahia e que os executivos ficaram impressionados com o potencial de ampliação da capacidade produtiva brasileira. “Para o Brasil, é uma capacidade enorme de poder expandir a produção de vanádio para uso em data centers aqui no Brasil”, disse. A aposta da mineradora é que a expansão dos data centers no país também possa estimular uma cadeia doméstica de armazenamento de energia, criando demanda para o mineral extraído em território brasileiro. Mina na Bahia e fornecimento aos EUA A Largo é uma companhia canadense com ações negociadas nas bolsas de Toronto e de Nova York. Seu principal ativo é a mina Maracás Menchen, localizada a cerca de 250 quilômetros de Salvador, que começou a produzir em 2014 e possui um dos depósitos de vanádio de maior teor do mundo. A operação é realizada a céu aberto e produz principalmente pentóxido de vanádio, composto utilizado na fabricação de ligas metálicas de alta resistência e como matéria-prima para outras aplicações industriais e energéticas. A importância estratégica do mineral também levou a Largo a ampliar sua atuação no mercado de defesa dos Estados Unidos. Em junho, a companhia foi selecionada para fornecer pentóxido de vanádio de alta pureza à DLA (Agência de Logística de Defesa dos Estados Unidos), responsável, entre outras atribuições, pela aquisição e formação de estoques de materiais estratégicos para o país. O contrato integra um programa de compras compartilhado com valor máximo de US$ 125 milhões e duração de cinco anos. Em julho, a Largo recebeu uma primeira encomenda de US$ 60,1 milhões, com entregas previstas até janeiro de 2030. O material produzido na Bahia será destinado aos estoques estratégicos americanos e poderá atender às necessidades da indústria de defesa, incluindo a fabricação de ligas metálicas utilizadas em equipamentos militares e aeronáuticos. Para Arias, o movimento reflete o interesse de países ocidentais em reduzir a dependência de fornecedores como China e Rússia em cadeias de minerais considerados críticos e estratégicos. O executivo defendeu que o vanádio receba maior atenção das políticas de minerais críticos, diante de suas aplicações na indústria de defesa, no setor aeroespacial e nas tecnologias de armazenamento de energia. Produção de cobre e expansão na Bahia Além do vanádio, a Largo começou a diversificar sua produção mineral na Bahia. Em agosto, a companhia iniciou a recuperação de concentrado de cobre associado a metais preciosos, após receber autorização da ANM (Agência Nacional de Mineração). O novo produto é obtido a partir do processamento de materiais da própria operação de Maracás Menchen e contém, além de cobre, elementos como ouro, platina, paládio e prata. Na prática, a mineradora passou a aproveitar outros minerais presentes no material extraído para produzir um concentrado comercializável, utilizando parte das instalações que já existiam na mina. Com a expansão das aplicações do vanádio e a diversificação para o cobre e metais preciosos, a Largo busca aumentar a rentabilidade de sua operação brasileira e aproveitar a demanda internacional por matérias-primas estratégicas.

artigo.texto: Promovido pelo fundo Aura Capital, através da Aura Technologies, que se apresenta como uma plataforma europeia de investimento e desenvolvimento focada em infraestrutura digital, o projeto prevê a instalação, no Parque Empresarial do Sorraia, do primeiro de uma rede de centros de dados “compactos” para treino e inferência de inteligência artificial (IA). A rede deverá estender-se a Espanha e ao sul de França, avançou o ECO. Com 6,4 MW, a capacidade ficará quase ao nível da do centro de dados da Covilhã. O objetivo é que a nova infraestrutura entre em funcionamento no final de 2027, empregando cerca de 30 pessoas. Segundo a informação publicada pelo SAPO, a empresa veículo para este projeto é a Nextgen AIDC Coruche, com sede na incubadora de empresas de Coruche, que pediu à Câmara Municipal que retirasse os ónus e encargos associados a um terreno no Parque Empresarial do Sorraia, avaliado em cerca de 180.000 mil euros. A proposta já foi aprovada em reunião do executivo, com os votos favoráveis dos três eleitos do PS e a abstenção dos quatro vereadores da oposição, do Movimento Volta Coruche e do PSD. O anúncio surge numa altura em que a associação ambientalista Quercus contabiliza 46 centros de dados já existentes em Portugal, 25 em Lisboa e 11 no Porto. O Governo admite poder vir a somar mais 44, quatro deles de grande dimensão, o que elevaria para 90 o número de infraestruturas deste tipo em território nacional.

artigo.texto: Nvidia Unveils DSX Pod for Faster AI Data Center Builds Nvidia said the DSX Pod, a prebuilt containerized AI data center, reduces deployment time from six months to 14 days. Nvidia today introduced DSX Pod, a containerized AI data center module that comes with seven Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, along with networking, cabling, and cooling already installed. The company says the design can cut deployment time at a prepared site from roughly six months to as little as 14 days. Announced at GTC Berlin, the modular offering is aimed at organizations that need to bring large amounts of AI compute online more quickly without going through the full planning, construction, and labor demands of a traditional on-site build. Nvidia said it is working with 17 partners, including Bull, Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo, Eaton, Schneider Electric, and Vertiv, to make DSX Pod available in early 2027. “This is a fully assembled, fully tested, fully pre-plumbed, prebuilt, pre-validated container that is the building block for AI factories,” said Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, in a media briefing. “It’s designed to accelerate Europe’s infrastructure deployment and dramatically shorten the time to first token.” Although Nvidia unveiled the reference design in Berlin, Buck said the container is intended for worldwide deployment. He said the company chose GTC Berlin for the announcement because it sees modular, faster-to-deploy infrastructure playing an important role in Europe’s expansion of AI capacity. Buck said the product is designed for organizations that want to bring compute online at the hundreds-of-megawatts scale more quickly while reducing the complexity of a conventional site build. Ashish Nadkarni, an IDC analyst, said the DSX Pod could be appealing for three use cases: sovereign AI deployments that require physical isolation, smaller-footprint AI deployments built for specific needs, and edge AI environments. “It provides accelerated compute capacity in a turnkey fashion wherever there is demand,” Nadkarni said. Manufacturing Expansion Targets AI Supply Bottlenecks The DSX Pod announcement came alongside a broader Nvidia update on manufacturing expansion. To support the growing demand for AI infrastructure, Nvidia and its supply chain partners said they plan to increase substrate capacity by 2.5 times over the next three years, expand advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by 2028, and increase optical engine capacity for co-packaged optics by 15 times by mid-2027, with a goal of doubling that again by the end of 2028. OpenShell Adds Governance for AI at Scale Nvidia also used the event to highlight software and security controls for AI deployments at scale. The company introduced the OpenShell Reference Architecture, which it said is designed to help organizations govern AI agents by defining what they can access and do, monitoring their behavior, and enforcing policies if unsafe activity is detected. Justin Boitano, Nvidia’s vice president of enterprise, said the architecture combines Vera Rubin NVL72 infrastructure for training and inference with Nvidia Vera systems that run and govern the “agent harness.” BlueField DPUs act as an isolated security monitor between the two systems, inspecting traffic and enabling policy updates that can disconnect an agent if unsafe behavior is detected. Nvidia said companies using the OpenShell Reference Architecture to strengthen agent security include Anthropic, AWS, Google Cloud, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Perplexity.

artigo.texto: Professor David S. Levine discusses trade secret protections, nondisclosure agreements and proposed federal legislation to improve public access to information around data centers. As Congress considers legislation to increase transparency in data center development, Elon University School of Law Professor David S. Levine recently discussed how trade secret protections and nondisclosure agreements can prevent the public from learning how taxpayer resources are used and how projects affect local communities. An Oct. 14 article published by MLex, “Trade secrets could constrain US legislative push to open data center deals,” examines the bipartisan No Secrets for Data Centers Act BILL, which would restrict non-disclosure agreements between data center developers and public officials. MLex, a LexisNexis news service, covers legal and regulatory developments for attorneys, businesses and government agencies. “The public expects transparency and accountability when it comes to allocation of taxpayer funds … NDAs piled on top of robust trade secret protection leaves the public largely blind. Given this compounded secrecy, the likelihood of corruption increases,” Levine told MLex. Levine, who studies trade secrecy and information law, also discusses how existing trade secret protections could continue to limit public access to information even if non-disclosure agreements were prohibited, preventing access to information about environmental, health, and safety risks and where public money is going. an area of focus, Levine was consulted by then-vice president Joe Biden’s staff regarding NDAs and trade secrecy during the second Obama administration. Read the full article at MLex. A subscription is required.

artigo.texto: Ten Reputable Solar Energy Storage Battery Manufacturers in China 2026: Advancing Clean Energy Storage Press Release Date 10-20-2026 A 2026 guide to ten reputable Chinese manufacturers of solar energy storage batteries. CALIFORNIA, CA, UNITED STATES, October 20, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- SHENZHEN, China, October 21, 2026 — Shenzhen Topway New Energy Co., Ltd., a lithium battery pack manufacturer based in Bao'an District, Shenzhen and trading as HCC, heads a ten-company editorial list of Chinese solar energy storage battery manufacturers published today. The list places the company alongside nine further Chinese battery producers whose storage products are sold in domestic and export markets. The review assesses companies on four criteria that are observable from public information: breadth of in-house research and engineering, certification coverage relevant to export markets, manufacturing footprint, and the range of storage applications served. It is an editorial assessment compiled from company information and third-party market data. It is not a third-party ranking, and no company paid for inclusion. The list is published as demand for battery energy storage systems expands. Grand View Research estimated the global Battery Energy Storage System market at approximately USD 13.2 billion in 2025, with a projected value of USD 99.7 billion by 2033, and reported that lithium-ion batteries accounted for 53.5% of the segment in 2025. Industry context: demand growth and tightening standards Storage demand is being shaped by two forces at once. The first is volume: utility, commercial and residential installations all require cell and pack supply, and the same cell chemistries now compete across all three. The second is standardisation, which changes what qualifies as a credible supplier. Three documents anchor the compliance side of the market. IEC 62619:2022 is the current international safety standard for lithium-ion batteries in industrial and stationary applications, and covers thermal runaway behaviour and battery management system verification. UL 1973 is the primary North American safety standard for batteries in stationary applications such as solar energy storage and uninterruptible power supplies. UN 38.3 governs the transport of lithium batteries globally and requires eight specific tests, including altitude simulation and thermal testing. Segment demand is uneven. Mordor Intelligence and Strategic Market Research estimated the global golf cart battery market at USD 1.49 billion in 2024, with lithium-ion types capturing a 47.18% share — a reminder that storage chemistries are displacing lead-acid in motive applications at the same time as they scale in stationary ones. How the ten companies were assessed The four criteria were applied consistently across all ten companies, and each company is described only on the basis of publicly stated business scope. The criteria are: Technical research and engineering. Whether a company operates its own development capability for cells, modules or packs, and whether that capability extends to custom configurations rather than catalogue-only products. Certification coverage. Whether products are documented against RoHS, CE, UL or equivalent schemes, since these determine access to European and North American channels. Manufacturing footprint. Plant area, headcount and production arrangements, used as an indicator of how much of the value chain a supplier controls directly. Application and solution breadth. The range of use cases served, from residential wall-mounted systems to golf cart traction packs, industrial backup and commercial peak-shaving configurations. No single criterion decides placement. Companies with large cell output but limited pack-level customisation are not treated as equivalent to companies that design and assemble complete packs for specific applications. The ten manufacturers 1. Shenzhen Topway New Energy Co., Ltd. (HCC) Founded in 2022, Shenzhen Topway New Energy operates from a 10,000 m² facility in Bao'an District, Shenzhen, with 200 employees and a 15-person R&D team, and states an export ratio of 40% across markets including the United States, Germany, Italy, Poland, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam and Australia. Its storage range covers the Wall-TW01 5 kW wall-mounted battery, built on LiFePO4 cells rated for at least 6,000 cycles at 80% capacity with a maximum continuous discharge current of 50 A; a 48 V 280 Ah solar battery pack rated at 200 A continuous discharge; a 51.2 V 200 Ah unit; 51.2 V 100 Ah and 48 V 100 Ah models; and 25.6 V 100 Ah and 12.8 V 100 Ah units. A 51.2 V 105 Ah pack serves golf cart traction. Products carry RoHS, UL and CE certification. The company states that it is moving from pack solutions and cooperative production toward in-house manufacturing with new production lines, and it also lists robot, exoskeleton and drone battery packs among its product lines — a breadth that supports custom pack engineering rather than single-format assembly. 2. Its position on the list reflects the depth of its cell engineering and its role as a cell supplier to system integrators, which places its products inside a large share of finished storage installations rather than only in direct-sale configurations. 3. artigo.texto: A Microsoft (MSFT) desistiu de um planejado data center de IA em Loughton, Essex, que o provedor britânico de nuvem Nscale estava construindo para ela, informou a Reuters em 18 de outubro, citando o Telegraph. A Microsoft é um dos dois maiores clientes da Nscale. A Reuters disse que o Telegraph não especificou o motivo da retirada da Microsoft, e a Microsoft declinou comentar o pedido da Reuters. O local realmente tinha um problema óbvio: energia. O Telegraph informou que os oficiais da rede disseram à Nscale que não esperavam fornecer eletricidade até a década de 2030. Isso corresponde a um relatório de setembro de que a UK Power Networks não conseguiria conectar o local antes do início a meados da década de 2030. A Nscale diz que permanece comprometida com Loughton e está analisando outras fontes de energia. Loughton Era uma Pequena Fatia da Expansão da Microsoft Loughton foi planejado para abrigar cerca de 23.000 chips da Nvidia (NVDA) para o Azure, começando com 50 MW. A Nscale concordou em fornecer à Microsoft cerca de 200.000 chips da Nvidia no Reino Unido, Noruega, Portugal e Texas, então Loughton representava cerca de 11,5% do programa. A Microsoft adicionou aproximadamente um gigawatt de capacidade apenas no trimestre de junho, o que faz com que a carga inicial de Loughton seja cerca de 5% de um trimestre. Os gastos não mostram sinais de recuo. Os gastos de capital em caixa atingiram US$ 35,80 bilhões no trimestre de junho, mais que o dobro dos US$ 17,08 bilhões de um ano antes. O capex em caixa do ano fiscal de 2026 totalizou US$ 115,95 bilhões, um aumento de cerca de 80%. Na medida mais ampla da administração, incluindo arrendamentos financeiros, o capex do trimestre de junho foi de aproximadamente US$ 41 bilhões, com mais de US$ 50 bilhões esperados no trimestre de setembro. A demanda está acompanhando o ritmo. A receita da Nuvem Inteligente atingiu US$ 39,31 bilhões no trimestre de junho, um aumento de cerca de 32% em relação aos US$ 29,88 bilhões, e a CFO Amy Hood disse que a demanda dos clientes ainda excede a oferta disponível. A Microsoft tem os clientes e o caixa. O que ela não consegue comprar rapidamente é eletricidade. Energia Primeiro, Depois os Chips A Microsoft já foi exigente com a Nscale antes. Ela assinou uma carta de intenção para até 1,35 GW no campus da Nscale na Virgínia Ocidental em março, depois desistiu durante o verão, e a Anthropic assumiu a capacidade. Enquanto isso, ela está pagando mais por locais com uma data de fornecimento de energia. Em 16 de outubro, dois dias antes do relatório sobre Loughton, a NiSource (NI) anunciou um acordo de 20 anos com a Microsoft, com o serviço previsto para começar em 2028 e aproximadamente 1.100 MW de recursos de geração a serem adicionados em Indiana. A outra solução alternativa é gerar energia no local, e é aí que entra a Bloom Energy (BE). A Nscale supostamente conversou com a Bloom sobre células de combustível para Loughton. A receita da Bloom atingiu um recorde de US$ 1,065 bilhão no trimestre de junho, um aumento de 166% em relação ao ano anterior. Seus últimos quatro trimestres renderam cerca de US$ 3,12 bilhões, quase o dobro dos US$ 1,63 bilhões dos quatro anteriores. Os atrasos na rede já estão aparecendo na demonstração de resultados de alguém. A saída prejudica muito mais a Nscale do que a Microsoft. O prospecto de IPO da Nscale lista acordos com a Microsoft no valor de até US$ 43,8 bilhões, e Loughton era seu principal local no Reino Unido. O Número que a Microsoft Divulga em 28 de Outubro A Microsoft divulga os resultados do primeiro trimestre fiscal após o fechamento em 28 de outubro. O capex incluindo arrendamentos financeiros é o número a ser verificado em relação à previsão de US$ 50 bilhões. Um valor acima de US$ 50 bilhões seria consistente com a orientação de gastos da Microsoft, mas não estabeleceria se os compromissos relacionados a Loughton foram redirecionados para outro lugar. Um valor mais baixo precisaria ser avaliado juntamente com a contabilidade de arrendamentos, o cronograma de entrega e a perspectiva de demanda da administração antes de concluir que a expansão está desacelerando. Não interpreto Loughton como a Microsoft perdendo o apetite por capacidade de IA, principalmente porque o trimestre de junho é difícil de conciliar com isso: o capex em caixa mais que dobrou ano a ano, a receita da Nuvem Inteligente cresceu cerca de 32%, e a Microsoft já tem 1.100 MW garantidos em Indiana a partir de 2028. O que ela parece ter perdido a paciência é com a data de conexão à rede de um local, não com a expansão. Até que 28 de outubro diga o contrário, estou tratando isso como uma história sobre energia. artigo.texto: Meta gives tour of Huntsville data center amid questions over energy, water use HUNTSVILLE, Ala. (WAFF) - Meta opened its Huntsville data center for a tour, highlighting the facility’s role in powering some of the company’s most widely used platforms as questions about data centers’ energy and water usage continue to draw attention nationwide. Meta’s Huntsville data center stores information used by platforms including Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, and supports the company’s AI applications. Henry Thornton, with Meta, said the center matches its electricity use with clean and renewable energy. When asked how much electricity the Huntsville facility uses, Thornton did not provide a specific figure. “Our electricity usage is something we don’t disclose at the exact megawatt level for our sub gigawatt facilities, but we match every megawatt we use with clean and renewable energy,” Thornton said. Thornton said the facility receives its power through the Tennessee Valley Authority. “What I’d say is that a Meta data center is not going to raise your electricity bill. We are responsible users of water,” Thornton said. He said the facility’s water comes from Huntsville Utilities. The company has pledged to become water-positive by 2030, but it did not provide specific water-use figures for the Huntsville facility. “People often have a very misconstrued idea about data centers and water usage. We, you know, really don’t use that much more than other industrial facilities or, you know, perhaps a golf course or something like that,” Thornton said. Meta leaders said they consider themselves active members of the Huntsville community and said the company has donated millions of dollars to Madison County initiatives. Meta is scheduled to give a presentation on the Huntsville facility at the Dec. 3 Huntsville City Council meeting. artigo.texto: Os Estados Unidos fecharam nesta terça-feira (21) uma parceria entre a americana Crusoe e a paraguaia Araico para construir um data center abastecido por energia da usina de Itaipu, na fronteira entre Brasil e Paraguai. O Brasil não foi citado no anúncio. O acordo foi firmado entre a Crusoe, que desenvolve infraestrutura de computação de alto desempenho, e a Araico, desenvolvedora paraguaia de projetos de energia. Segundo o Departamento de Estado dos EUA, a 1ª fase da instalação deve entrar em operação em meados de 2027. O anúncio aconteceu durante visita do vice-secretário de Estado americano, Christopher Landau, ao Paraguai. A viagem foi entre segunda (19) e quarta (21). Landau se reuniu com o presidente Santiago Peña e com o chanceler Rubén Ramírez Lezcano. O interesse americano não é novo. Em maio de 2025, o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, já defendia esse tipo de parceria no Senado dos EUA. "Temos que discutir como investiremos em países que têm um suprimento de energia capaz de atender a essa demanda. Como, por exemplo, o Paraguai", disse Rubio à Comissão de Relações Exteriores do Senado americano. Por que o Brasil não participa do acordo? O Brasil ficou de fora porque, desde 1973, o Tratado de Itaipu reservava ao país a exclusividade sobre o excedente de energia não consumido pelo Paraguai. Um acordo de 2025 revisou essa regra e autorizou os paraguaios a vender energia diretamente a terceiros. A energia de Itaipu é dividida meio a meio entre os dois países, mas o Paraguai usa só parte da própria cota. O consumo interno paraguaio passou de 10% em 2012 para mais de 30% em 2024. Publicidade Na prática, a decisão sobre o excedente deixou de depender de negociação bilateral com o Brasil. O restante do excedente agora pode ir a clientes como a Crusoe. Enquanto isso, o Brasil vive expansão própria de data centers, com projetos que também miram energia barata e abundante. O tema virou consenso entre os presidenciáveis na eleição deste ano, que defendem atrair mais investimento do setor para o país. A relação entre Brasil e Paraguai já vinha de atrito. Em julho, o país vizinho entregou nota de repúdio ao embaixador brasileiro por causa de uma fala do presidente Lula sobre a Guerra do Paraguai. Reportagens do setor elétrico apontam que autoridades brasileiras já tratam o fim dessa exclusividade como risco. O temor é perder previsibilidade no fornecimento e poder de barganha regional diante do Paraguai. O que acontece agora A primeira fase da instalação movida a Itaipu deve entrar em operação em meados de 2027, segundo o Departamento de Estado dos EUA. O comunicado americano não revelou o valor do investimento nem o volume de energia contratado. O acordo é parte de uma ofensiva maior dos EUA no Paraguai. A americana Uranium Energy Corp. também anunciou investimento de US$ 12 milhões numa concessão de urânio, e os dois países assinaram acordo de assistência para interceptação aérea.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Daily presents a selection of the latest developments from China's automotive industry. Here are the key stories in this edition. BYD Brings Flash Charging to Indonesia with New DENZA Models BYD introduced its second-generation Blade Battery and Flash Charging technology in Indonesia, marking the technology's overseas debut. The announcement coincided with the launch of two new DENZA models, the D9 and the Z9GT, as BYD expands its electric vehicle lineup and charging services in the Southeast Asian market. According to BYD, its Flash Charging technology can charge a battery from 10% to 70% in as little as five minutes, and from 10% to 97% in nine minutes under normal conditions. The system integrates energy storage with charging equipment and features a lightweight charging connector designed to make plugging in easier, as well as a plug-and-charge function. To support the rollout, BYD plans to install Flash Charging equipment at 10 DENZA dealerships in Indonesia in the initial phase. The stations will be open to the public, providing an initial charging network before the company expands coverage further. The new DENZA D9 comes equipped with the second-generation Blade Battery and Flash Charging technology, alongside upgrades to powertrain performance, driving range and comfort. The Z9GT, meanwhile, is built on BYD's e³ platform, extending the brand's premium electric vehicle offering in Indonesia. Huawei-Backed Yinwang Teams Up with CATL on Automated Battery Swapping Yinwang Intelligent Technology, a Huawei-affiliated smart vehicle company, has signed a strategic cooperation agreement with CATL and its battery-swapping subsidiary, Contemporary Amperex Energy Service Technology, to develop an intelligent battery-swapping ecosystem for autonomous vehicles. The agreement was signed on October 19 and covers vehicle integration, swappable batteries and network development. The three companies plan to connect vehicles, battery-swapping stations and cloud systems, using real-time battery data and drivers' travel patterns to predict energy needs and coordinate services. The proposed system would allow vehicles to determine when a battery swap is needed, locate a station, enter and align automatically, complete the swap in just 99 seconds, and drive away without human intervention. The partnership brings Yinwang into CATL's Choco-Swap ecosystem. The companies will adapt participating vehicle models to work with the network, with the aim of expanding access to battery-swapping services for vehicles equipped with Huawei's Qiankun intelligent automotive solutions. CATL's Choco-Swap network had 2,520 stations across 200 Chinese cities as of September 29. The company plans to expand the network to 30,000 stations and connect urban and highway coverage, although the announcement did not specify a timeline for reaching that target. The deal highlights how Chinese companies are working to integrate automated driving with energy replenishment. By linking vehicle intelligence, cloud-based service coordination and battery-swapping infrastructure, the partners aim to make battery replacement faster and more convenient while extending the service network available to intelligent vehicles. Schaeffler Opens Humanoid Robot Factory in China Schaeffler opened a humanoid robotics factory in Taicang, Jiangsu province, on October 20, bringing robot-component manufacturing, robot training and industrial applications together under one roof. Spanning approximately 7,500 square meters, the facility is designed to help move humanoid robots from experimental projects into real-world manufacturing. Six humanoid robots are already working on an assembly line producing joint modules for other humanoid robots. Across five workstations, they handle tasks including material handling, parts sorting, press-fitting, inspection and packaging. The setup marks a step toward a closed manufacturing loop in which humanoid robots help produce components for the next generation of robots. The factory also includes dedicated training environments for industrial tasks such as visual inspection, material picking and component assembly. A digital-twin system connects robot training with production validation and process optimization, allowing Schaeffler to test and refine processes virtually before implementing changes on the actual production line. The opening comes as Schaeffler expands its humanoid robotics business in China. The company said it secured orders from two new Chinese customers in the third quarter of 2026, bringing its cumulative global order intake in humanoid robotics to approximately €400 million. The Taicang facility will also serve as a platform for collaboration with Chinese robotics companies.

artigo.texto: The 13-member Lancaster County Data Center Task Force met for the first time Tuesday to set expectations and goals for its six scheduled meetings, during which members will study data center regulations and develop recommendations for the Lancaster County Board. The group will govern the development of data centers in rural Lancaster County. “I cannot express my gratitude for you taking on this assignment,” Lancaster County Commissioner Christa Yoakum said. “This is going to take up a chunk of your lives from now until the end of the year, when we hope that you’re able to have a recommendation, or some recommendations to bring forward to us.” The County Board nixed a potential 12-month data center moratorium in favor of the task force. Currently, at least four cities — Lincoln, Omaha, Kearney and Papillion — and eight counties — including Cass, Gage and Seward — have moratoriums on data centers. As part of the inaugural meeting — which was led by David Cary, director of Lincoln-Lancaster County Planning and Development Services, who is not a member of the task force — each of the 12 members present was asked to share their goals, which included making policy, supporting the community and setting baselines. “I want to protect public health safety and welfare,” said John Hansen, president of the Nebraska Farmers Union. “But I also want to come up with a balanced set of rules and regulations.” The task force also laid groundwork for the months ahead, including going over county and zoning regulations. Currently, there are no data centers in rural Lancaster County. However, two companies have bought land for potential centers — though Cary said the county has not had any discussions yet about either. West of Hallam, Sagebrush Infrastructure Partners, which builds hyperscale data centers and natural gas-fired power plants, entered into the agreements for about 1,700 acres of land valued at about $10.35 million, according to documents from the Lancaster County Assessor’s Office. The purchase agreements — involving at least 11 landowners and 21 parcels of land — were signed between December and March, according to the assessor's office. These agreements give Sagebrush an exclusivity period ranging between 2½ and four years into the future to purchase the land at an agreed-upon price. A representative for Stark Power, the Israeli-owned company that acquired Sagebrush in June, said the company is exploring the possibility of developing a data center in the area, though no final decision has been made. The project could be a 1.7-gigawatt hyperscale campus, enough to power 1.3 million homes. And just outside of Lincoln, Coffee Grounds Data LLC, registered in Delaware, agreed to a purchase agreement for about 560 acres worth $3.46 million with landowner Larry Coffey in September, according to property records. The land sits off U.S. 34 and Nebraska 79 less than five miles east of Malcolm. Signing the deal for the data company was Ricardo Graf, chief development officer and managing partner at Arevia Power, a San Francisco-based company known for its solar power projects. More recently, the company, through subsidiary Rhea Data, has delved into data centers, proposing a 600-megawatt facility on public land in Idaho, which could be the state’s largest. Graf and Arevia were also connected to a project in Adair, Okla., a town about 45 minutes northeast of Tulsa. Two community members who live by the potential Arevia data center spoke during the task force’s public hearing. Nate Tederman, who lives in Malcolm, said he was unhappy with his community’s lack of representation. “Our voices aren’t getting heard. We’re the community out there,” he said. “I couldn’t be more against it.” On the other hand, Adam Hohbein, whose land neighbors where the potential data center could be, said he was not fully opposed to the project, but hoped the task force weighed it carefully. “I really want to make sure that we’re taking into consideration the people that are existing residents,” he said. “I just want to make sure that we’re being diligent about how we’re going about this process and what kind of regulations we set on them.” The task force will meet again Nov. 3. Its final meeting is expected to be on Jan. 5, though its timeline could be extended if necessary. Another data center task force, put together by Gov. Jim Pillen and overseen by the Nebraska Department of Water, Energy and Environment, held its second meeting in Columbus on Tuesday. Made up of 19 members including the CEOs of Lincoln Electric System, the Nebraska Public Power District and the Omaha Public Power District, Pillen’s task force is expected to meet again in Lincoln on Nov. 19. © 2026 Lincoln Journal Star, Neb. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

artigo.texto: Yasin Gungor 21 October 2026•Update: 21 October 2026 US President Donald Trump on Wednesday urged operators of large artificial intelligence data centers to strike financial agreements with local communities and pay them dividends to ease public backlash over rising energy costs. "If companies want to make their data centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a 'dividend,'" Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social, arguing that projects facing fierce local opposition quickly gain acceptance once direct economic pacts are reached. Trump said facilities must produce their own power rather than draining public utilities. He maintained that new and large data centers are required to "make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid," asserting that such measures would prevent utility inflation and potentially yield "a substantial decrease" in electricity rates. The US has more than 5,000 data centers, with facilities projected to expand roughly 9% annually through 2030, according to the US Department of Commerce. The directive comes amid escalating friction over power consumption driven by the artificial intelligence boom ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Public surveys show strong bipartisan opposition, with a Gallup poll finding 71% of Americans resisting local developments over concerns that facilities will inflate residential utility bills. The policy builds upon Trump's voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge established in March, which called on technology firms to cover all power generation and transmission costs.

artigo.texto: Home › Energy Storage ›Sahaj Solar to Establish 1.8 GWh BESS Manufacturing Facility in Gujarat Sahaj Solar to Establish 1.8 GWh BESS Manufacturing Facility in Gujarat Sahaj Solar has approved an investment of approximately INR 25 crore to set up a 1.8 GWh BESS manufacturing facility in Dakor, Gujarat, within 12 months. October 21, 2026. By Mrinmoy Dey Gujarat-based Sahaj Solar has announced that the company’s Board of Directors has approved a proposal to set up a new Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing facility with a production and storage capacity of 1.8 GWh at Dakor, Gujarat, with an investment of approximately INR 25 crore. The facility is expected to be set up within 12 months, with the investment to be financed through debt and internal accruals. The estimated investment excludes the cost of the factory premises, which have already been constructed, the company stated in a regulatory filing. The proposed facility will manufacture BESS for domestic and international markets. The company stated that the investment is aimed at vertically integrating its existing solar systems business. The proposed facility will mark Sahaj Solar’s entry into BESS manufacturing, with a planned capacity of 1.8 GWh. artigo.texto: GREEN CHARTER TOWNSHIP, Mich. (Michigan News Source) – After years of controversy, lawsuits and political battles, the proposed Gotion electric vehicle battery plant in Mecosta County is heading toward a legal conclusion. And the current price tag for settling one federal claim? One dollar. Township Approves Settlement The Green Charter Township Board of Trustees approved a proposed settlement agreement on Thursday, October 15 during a special meeting, potentially ending litigation involving Gotion Inc. and its controversial battery plant project. MORE NEWS: Trump Calls Slotkin a ‘Lowlife’ Over Remarks About Young Trump Administration Recruits According to the Big Rapids Pioneer, the agreement requires Gotion to transfer the proposed project property to the Michigan State Land Bank. The Michigan Strategic Fund would also drop its demand against Gotion involving grant funds. The township would refund certain project-related funds and remove some public statements concerning Gotion, the litigation, and economic development organization The Right Place. One Dollar and Done? Under the agreement, Gotion would receive a consent judgment on one federal claim with just $1 in damages. All remaining claims would be dismissed with prejudice, preventing them from being refiled. The parties would also terminate project agreements and release claims against one another related to the dispute. Township attorney Kyle O’Meara said the agreement follows negotiations culminating in an October 2 settlement conference before a federal magistrate judge. Although the township has approved the terms, final paperwork may still require additional board approval. MORE NEWS: Political Signs Spark Owosso Farmers Market Showdown; GOP Alleges Double Standard For residents who fought the controversial project, the proposed settlement signals that the long-running battle over the battery plant is finally moving toward a conclusion. Cella: Gotion Deal Was a Threat to National Security Joseph Cella, director and co-founder of the Michigan China Economic Security and Review Group, who has been a vocal opponent of the Gotion battery plant project, called the agreement between government officials and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)-linked company corrupt from the beginning. He said in a statement to Michigan News Source, “It moved fast and in secret and it ruptured the consent of the governed,” He accused officials of failing to conduct proper due diligence and ignoring national security concerns, describing the project as having “all of the textbook markings of a subnational incursion and influence operation by a CCP-tied entity.” Cella credited local residents for defeating the project, saying it would not have happened without the patriots of Mecosta County who “courageously stood up, exposed it, tenaciously fought it, and ultimately restored the consent of the governed.”
